title.en: Volume 112 Biographies 37: Wang, Han, Su, Xue, Wang, Liu, Feng, Jiang
title.raw: 卷一百一十二 列傳第三十七 王韓蘇薛王柳馮蔣 Volume 112 Biographies 37: Wang, Han, Su, Xue, Wang, Liu, Feng, Jiang

sentences.zh: 王韓蘇薛王柳馮蔣

translations.literal: Wang, Han, Su, Xue, Wang, Liu, Feng, Jiang
translations.idiomatic: Wang, Han, Su, Xue, Wang, Liu, Feng, and Jiang

translations.literal: 1.2.1 Shi Baozhong
translations.idiomatic: 1.2.1 Shi Baozhong

translations.literal: 1.2.2 Qiu Yue
translations.idiomatic: 1.2.2 Qiu Yue

sentences.zh: 王義方，泗州漣水人，客於魏。

translations.literal: Wang Yifang was a native of Lianshui in Sizhou and lived as a sojourner in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yifang was a native of Lianshui in Sizhou and lived as a sojourner in Wei.

sentences.zh: 孤且窶，事母謹甚。

translations.literal: He was orphaned and poor, and he served his mother with the utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned and poor, and he served his mother with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 淹究經術，性謇特，高自標樹。

translations.literal: He deeply studied the classics and their methods; by nature he was outspoken and singular, setting a high standard for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply studied the classics and their methods; by nature he was outspoken and singular, setting a high standard for himself.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，詣京師，客有徒步疲於道者，自言：「父宦遠方，病且革，欲往省，困不能前。」

translations.literal: Recommended for the Mingjing examination, he went to the capital. There was a traveler on foot, exhausted on the road, who said of himself, “My father serves in office in a distant region and is gravely ill. I wish to go inquire after him, but I am worn out and cannot go forward.”
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the Mingjing examination, he went to the capital. There was a traveler on foot, exhausted on the road, who said of himself, “My father serves in office in a distant region and is gravely ill. I wish to go inquire after him, but I am worn out and cannot go forward.”

sentences.zh: 義方哀之，解所乘馬以遺，不告姓名去，由是譽振一時。

translations.literal: Yifang pitied him, gave him the horse he was riding, and left without giving his name. Because of this, his reputation shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang pitied him, gave him the horse he was riding, and left without giving his name. Because of this, his reputation shook the age.

sentences.zh: 不肯造請貴勢，太宗使宰相聽其論。

translations.literal: He refused to visit and petition the powerful, so Taizong had the chancellors listen to his arguments.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to visit and petition the powerful, so Taizong had the chancellors listen to his arguments.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書外郎獨孤悊以儒顯，給事中許敬宗推悊確論，義方引逮百家異同，連拄悊，直出其上。

translations.literal: At the time, Dugu Zhe, Yuanwailang in the Department of State Affairs, was prominent as a classicist, and the Supervising Secretary Xu Jingzong promoted Zhe’s firm arguments; Yifang cited the agreements and disagreements of the hundred schools, repeatedly checked Zhe, and plainly surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Dugu Zhe, Yuanwailang in the Department of State Affairs, was prominent as a classicist, and the Supervising Secretary Xu Jingzong promoted Zhe’s firm arguments; Yifang cited the agreements and disagreements of the hundred schools, repeatedly checked Zhe, and plainly surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 左右爲悊不平，輒罷會。

translations.literal: Those nearby felt the result was unfair to Zhe and abruptly ended the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Those nearby felt the result was unfair to Zhe and abruptly ended the gathering.

sentences.zh: 補晉王府參軍，直弘文館。

translations.literal: Yifang was appointed staff officer in the Prince of Jin’s household and served on duty at the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang was appointed staff officer in the Prince of Jin’s household and served on duty at the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 魏徵異之，欲妻以夫人之侄，辭不取。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng considered him extraordinary and wanted to marry him to his wife’s niece, but Yifang declined and did not take her.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng considered him extraordinary and wanted to marry him to his wife’s niece, but Yifang declined and did not take her.

sentences.zh: 俄而徵薨，乃取女。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zheng died, and only then did Yifang marry the woman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zheng died, and only then did Yifang marry the woman.

sentences.zh: 人問其然，曰：「初不附宰相，今感知己故也。」

translations.literal: When someone asked why, he said, “At first I would not attach myself to a chancellor; now I am moved by one who understood me.”
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, he said, “At first I would not attach myself to a chancellor; now I am moved by one who understood me.”

sentences.zh: 素善張亮，亮抵罪，故貶吉安丞。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Zhang Liang. When Liang was punished for his crime, [Yifang] was therefore demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Zhang Liang. When Zhang was condemned for his offense, Yifang was demoted to assistant magistrate of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 道南海，舟師持酒脯請福，義方酌水誓曰：「有如忠獲戾，孝見尤，四維廓氛，千里安流。

translations.literal: Traveling the route to the Southern Sea, the boatmen brought wine and dried meat to seek blessings. Yifang poured water and swore, saying: "If loyalty should bear blame and filial piety meet reproach, may the four cardinal virtues clear the miasma, and may a thousand li of waters flow in peace.
translations.idiomatic: On the voyage south to the sea, the boatmen brought wine and dried meat to seek divine favor. Yifang poured water instead and vowed: "If loyalty must be punished and filial devotion blamed, may the four cardinal virtues dispel the foul vapors and calm the waters for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 神之聽之，無作神羞。」

translations.literal: O spirits, hear this — bring no shame upon the gods.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits, hear me — do not bring disgrace upon yourselves."

sentences.zh: 是時盛夏，濤霧蒸湧，既祭，天雲開露。

translations.literal: At that time it was the height of summer; billows and mist steamed and surged. After the offering, the sky opened and dew appeared.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer; waves and mist boiled up around them. When the rite was finished, the clouds parted and clear sky broke through.

sentences.zh: 人壯其誠。

translations.literal: People were awed by his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it were moved by the force of his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 吉安介蠻夷，梗悍不馴，義方召首領，稍選生徒，為開陳經書，行釋奠禮，清歌吹，登降跽立，人人悅順。

translations.literal: Ji'an bordered the barbarian Yi lands; the people were obstinate, fierce, and hard to tame. Yifang summoned their chiefs, gradually selected students, expounded the classics for them, performed the libation sacrifice rite, with clear singing and music — ascending, descending, kneeling and standing — until everyone came to delight in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an lay on the edge of the southern barbarian lands, where the people were stubborn and wild. Yifang summoned their leaders, chose students among them, and opened the classics to their hearing. He performed the libation sacrifice, with clear song and music; as men ascended and descended, knelt and rose, one and all came to take pleasure in order.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙洹水丞。

translations.literal: After some time, he was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to assistant magistrate of Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 而亮兄子皎自朱崖還，依義方。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Zhang Liang's elder brother's son Jiao returned from Zhuyai and relied on Yifang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang's elder brother's son Jiao returned from Zhuyai and came to live under Yifang's care.

sentences.zh: 將死，諉妻子，願以屍歸葬，義方許之。

translations.literal: As he was dying, he entrusted his wife and children, expressing the wish that his corpse be returned for burial. Yifang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao was near death, he entrusted his wife and children to Yifang and asked that his body be carried home for burial. Yifang promised.

sentences.zh: 以皎妻少，故與之誓於神，使奴負柩，輟馬載皎妻，身步從之。

translations.literal: Because Jiao's wife was young, he therefore made a vow before the spirits with her; he had a servant carry the coffin, gave up his horse to carry Jiao's wife, and himself walked behind.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiao's wife was still young, Yifang swore an oath before the spirits in her presence: a servant bore the coffin, he gave up his horse for Jiao's wife, and he himself walked on foot behind them.

sentences.zh: 既葬皎原武，歸妻其家，而告亮墓乃去。

translations.literal: After burying Jiao at Yuanwu, he returned the wife to her family, paid respects at Zhang Liang's tomb, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: After burying Jiao at Yuanwu, he restored the wife to her family, paid his respects at Zhang Liang's grave, and only then took his leave.

sentences.zh: 遷雲陽丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，擢侍御史，不再旬，會李義府縱大理囚婦淳於，迫其丞畢正義縊死，無敢白其奸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, he was promoted to Attending Censor. Within less than ten days, it happened that Li Yifu released the prisoner Chunyu of the Court of Judicial Review and forced Vice Magistrate Bi Zhengyi to hang himself; no one dared report the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he was raised to attending censor. Within ten days, Li Yifu had a woman named Chunyu released from the Court of Judicial Review and forced Vice Magistrate Bi Zhengyi to hang himself. No one dared expose the crime.

sentences.zh: 義方自以興縣屬，不三時拜御史，且疾當世附離匪人以欺朝廷，內決劾奏，意必得罪，即問計於母。

translations.literal: Yifang, considering himself a subject of Xing County who had become censor in less than three seasons, and hating that men of his day clung to evil men to deceive the court, resolved inwardly to impeach and submit a memorial, knowing he would surely be punished — and so he asked his mother's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang, a man of Xing County who had become censor in less than a year, loathed how men of the age clung to wicked patrons to deceive the throne. He resolved to impeach Li Yifu, knowing he would surely be punished, and went to ask his mother's advice.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「昔王母伏劍，成陵之誼。

translations.literal: His mother said: "Long ago the Queen Mother drew her sword — the righteousness of protecting the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Long ago the Queen Mother drew her sword — such was the righteousness of guarding the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 汝能盡忠，吾願之，死不恨。」

translations.literal: If you can give your full loyalty, that is my wish; I shall die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you can give your full loyalty, that is all I ask. I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 義方即上言：「天子置公卿大夫士，欲水火相濟，鹽梅相成，不得獨是獨非也。

translations.literal: Yifang thereupon submitted a memorial: "The Son of Heaven appoints lords, ministers, grand masters, and officers so that water and fire may complement each other and salt and sour plum may together bring seasoning — one may not uphold only what is right or only what is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang thereupon submitted a memorial: "The Son of Heaven appoints lords, ministers, grandees, and officers so that water and fire may complement each other, salt and sour plum may together season a dish — a ruler must not hear only agreement and never dissent.

sentences.zh: 昔堯失之四凶，漢高祖失之陳豨，光武失之逄萌，魏武失之張邈。

translations.literal: Of old Yao lost the Four Evildoers, Han Gaozu lost Chen Xi, Emperor Guangwu lost Pang Meng, and Cao Cao lost Zhang Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Yao lost the Four Evildoers, Han Gaozu lost Chen Xi, Emperor Guangwu lost Pang Meng, and Cao Cao lost Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 彼聖傑之主，然皆失於前而得於後。

translations.literal: Those sagely and heroic rulers all erred at first yet recovered afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Those were sage and heroic rulers, yet each erred at first and only set things right afterward.

sentences.zh: 今陛下撫萬邦而有之，蠻區夷落，罪無逃罰，況輦轂下奸臣肆虐乎？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty pacifies the myriad states and holds them all; in remote barbarian regions no crime escapes punishment — how much less under the imperial chariot hub may wicked ministers run rampant!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty holds the myriad realms in peace; even in the farthest barbarian districts no crime escapes punishment — how then can wicked ministers run riot beneath the imperial chariot?

sentences.zh: 殺人滅口，此生殺之柄，不自主出，而下移佞臣，履霜堅冰，彌不可長。

translations.literal: To kill men and silence mouths — the power over life and death no longer proceeds from the sovereign's own hand but has shifted down to sycophantic ministers; tread on frost and solid ice follows — this must not be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: To kill a man and silence his mouth — the power of life and death no longer issues from Your Majesty's own hand but has passed down to sycophantic ministers. Tread on frost and solid ice follows; this cannot be allowed to go on.

sentences.zh: 請下有司雜治正義死狀。」

translations.literal: I beg that the matter be referred to the relevant offices for joint investigation of the circumstances of Zhengyi's death.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the matter be referred to the proper offices for a full inquiry into the circumstances of Zhengyi's death."

sentences.zh: 即具法冠對伏，叱義府下，跪讀所言。

translations.literal: Immediately he donned the law cap and bowed prostrate, shouted for Yifu to come down, and knelt to read aloud what he had written.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately donned the censor's cap and bowed prostrate, ordered Yifu to come down from the dais, and knelt to read his accusation aloud.

sentences.zh: 帝方安義府狡佞，恨義方以孤士觸宰相，貶萊州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then content with Yifu's cunning flattery and resented that Yifang, a lone scholar, had crossed the chief minister; Yifang was demoted to Registrar of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then well pleased with Yifu's cunning sycophancy and resented that Yifang, a lone scholar, had crossed the chief minister. Yifang was demoted to registrar of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲終不復調，往客昌樂，聚徙教授。

translations.literal: At year's end he was no longer reassigned; he went to live as a guest in Changle, gathering disciples and instructing them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the year he received no new appointment. He went to live in Changle as a guest, gathering disciples and teaching.

sentences.zh: 母喪，隱居不出。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he went into seclusion and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he withdrew into seclusion and did not emerge again.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 義方為御史時，買第，後數日，愛廷中樹，復召主人曰：「此佳樹，得無欠償乎？」

translations.literal: When Yifang was censor, he bought a residence; several days later, he grew fond of a tree in the courtyard, summoned the former owner again and said: "This is a fine tree — surely it was not left unpaid for?
translations.idiomatic: When Yifang was censor he bought a house. Several days later, taken with a tree in the courtyard, he summoned the former owner and said, "This is a fine tree — surely you were not left unpaid for it?"

sentences.zh: 又予之錢。

translations.literal: He also gave him money."
translations.idiomatic: He paid him for it as well.

sentences.zh: 其廉不貪類此。

translations.literal: His integrity and freedom from greed were of this kind throughout.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and freedom from greed were like this in all things.

sentences.zh: 始，魏征愛其材也，每恨太直，後卒以疾惡不容於時。

translations.literal: From the start Wei Zheng admired his talent but always regretted that he was too blunt; in the end he perished because his hatred of evil could not be tolerated in that age.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Wei Zheng admired his talent but always regretted that he was too blunt. In the end he died because his fierce hatred of evil could not be borne in that age.

sentences.zh: 既死，門人員半千、何彥先行喪，蒔松柏冢側，三年乃去。

translations.literal: After his death, his disciples Yuan Banqian and He Yanxian performed mourning rites, planted pine and cypress at the grave's side, and only departed after three years.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his disciples Yuan Banqian and He Yanxian observed mourning for him, planted pine and cypress beside the grave, and did not leave until three years had passed.

sentences.zh: 何彥先

translations.literal: He Yanxian
translations.idiomatic: He Yanxian

sentences.zh: 彥先，齊州全節人。

translations.literal: Yanxian was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxian was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 武后時，位天官侍郎。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign he held the post of Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Officials.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign he served as vice minister of the Bureau of Celestial Officials.

sentences.zh: 員半千

translations.literal: Yuan Banqian
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Banqian

sentences.zh: 員半千，字榮期，齊州全節人。

translations.literal: Yuan Banqian, courtesy name Rongqi, was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Banqian, courtesy name Rongqi, was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 其先本彭城劉氏，十世祖凝之，事宋，起部郎，及齊受禪，奔元魏，以忠烈自比伍員，因賜姓員，終鎮西將軍、平涼郡公。

translations.literal: His forebears were originally of the Liu clan of Pengcheng. His tenth-generation ancestor Ningzhi served the Song, as Director of the Bureau of Personnel; when Qi received the abdication he fled to Northern Wei, likening his loyalty and valor to Wu Zixu, and was granted the surname Yuan. He ended as General Who Guards the West and Duke of Pingliang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were originally of the Liu clan of Pengcheng. His tenth-generation ancestor Ningzhi served the Song as director of the Bureau of Personnel; when Qi received the abdication he fled to Northern Wei, likening his loyalty and valor to Wu Zixu, and was granted the surname Yuan. He ended his career as General Who Guards the West and Duke of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 半千始名餘慶，生而孤，為從父鞠愛，鹴草通書史。

translations.literal: Banqian was originally named Yuqing. Orphaned from birth, he was raised with affection by his father's younger cousin; by the age of nine he was versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Banqian was originally named Yuqing. Orphaned from birth, he was raised with affection by his father's younger cousin; by the age of nine he was versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 客晉州，州舉童子，房玄齡異之，對詔高第，已能講《易》、《老子》。

translations.literal: While lodging in Jinzhou, the prefecture recommended him as a youth prodigy; Fang Xuanling was impressed, and in the imperial examination he placed at the top, already able to expound the Book of Changes and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: While staying in Jinzhou, the prefecture recommended him as a youth prodigy. Fang Xuanling was struck by him, and in the imperial examination he placed at the top, already able to lecture on the Book of Changes and the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 長與何彥先同事王義方，以邁秀見賞。

translations.literal: As he grew up he studied together with He Yanxian under Wang Yifang and was admired for his outstanding excellence.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he studied with He Yanxian under Wang Yifang and was admired for his surpassing excellence.

sentences.zh: 義方常曰：「五百歲一賢者生，子宜當之。」

translations.literal: Yifang often said: "Once every five hundred years a sage is born — you should be that one.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang often said, "Once every five hundred years a sage is born — you ought to be that one."

sentences.zh: 因改今名。

translations.literal: On this account he changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he took his present name.

sentences.zh: 凡舉八科，皆中。

translations.literal: In all eight examination categories he passed.
translations.idiomatic: He entered all eight civil-service examinations and passed every one.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，上書自陳：「臣家貲不滿千錢，有田三十畝，粟五十石。

translations.literal: During the Xianheng era he submitted a memorial stating himself: "My household property does not reach a thousand cash; I have thirty mou of land and fifty shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng era he submitted a memorial in his own person: "My household wealth does not amount to a thousand cash. I have thirty mou of land and fifty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 聞陛下封神嶽，舉豪英，故鬻錢走京師。

translations.literal: Hearing that Your Majesty was performing the feng sacrifice at the sacred peak and selecting heroic talents, I therefore sold my possessions and hastened to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Your Majesty was performing the feng sacrifice at the sacred peak and selecting outstanding men, I sold what I had and hurried to the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷九品無葭莩親，行年三十，懷誌潔操，未蒙一官，不能陳力歸報天子。

translations.literal: In the nine ranks of the court I have no kin even by the most distant tie; at thirty years of age, cherishing lofty resolve and pure integrity, I have yet to receive a single office — I cannot display my strength and repay the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the nine ranks of the court I have no kin even by the remotest tie. At thirty, with lofty resolve and unsullied conduct, I have yet to receive a single post — I cannot offer my strength in repayment to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 陛下何惜玉陛方寸地，不使臣披露肝膽乎？

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty grudge a hand's breadth of the jade steps and not allow me to lay bare my heart and liver?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty grudge a hand's breadth of the jade steps and not allow me to lay bare my heart?

sentences.zh: 得天下英才五千，與榷所長，有一居先，臣當伏死都市。」

translations.literal: Gather five thousand outstanding talents from the realm and weigh their strengths; if any one ranks ahead of me, let me be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Gather five thousand outstanding men from the realm and weigh their strengths against mine; if any one ranks ahead of me, let me be executed in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 書奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 調武陟尉，歲旱，勸令殷子良發粟振民，不從。

translations.literal: Assigned as magistrate of Wuzhi, in a year of drought he urged the prefect Yin Ziliang to release grain to relieve the people; Yin would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as magistrate of Wuzhi, in a year of drought he urged the prefect Yin Ziliang to open the granaries and relieve the people. Yin refused.

sentences.zh: 及子良謁州，半千悉發之，下賴以濟。

translations.literal: When Ziliang went to pay respects at the prefecture, Banqian released all the grain; the people below relied on this to survive.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziliang went up to the prefectural seat on business, Banqian released all the grain, and the people below were saved by it.

sentences.zh: 刺史大怒，囚半千於獄。

translations.literal: The censor was furious and imprisoned Banqian.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was furious and had Banqian thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 會薛元超持節度河，讓太守曰：「君有民不能恤，使惠出一尉，尚可罪邪？」

translations.literal: It happened that Xue Yuanchao arrived bearing credentials to oversee the Yellow River region and reproached the prefect: "You have the people yet cannot care for them, while a single magistrate dispenses kindness — can that be a crime?
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Xue Yuanchao arrived with imperial credentials to oversee the Yellow River region and reproached the prefect: "You have charge of the people yet cannot care for them, while a single magistrate dispenses relief — can that be a crime?"

sentences.zh: 釋之。

translations.literal: Banqian was released.
translations.idiomatic: Banqian was released.

sentences.zh: 俄舉嶽牧，高宗禦武成殿，問：「兵家有三陣，何謂邪？」

translations.literal: Soon recommended as prefectural governor; Emperor Gaozong presided at Wucheng Hall and asked: "Military strategists speak of three formations — what do they mean?
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recommended in the prefectural-governor examination. Emperor Gaozong presided at Wucheng Hall and asked, "Military strategists speak of three formations — what are they?"

sentences.zh: 眾未對，半千進曰：「臣聞古者星宿孤虛，天陣也；

translations.literal: No one answered. Banqian stepped forward: "I have heard that in antiquity the star positions of Gu and Xu formed the celestial formation;
translations.idiomatic: No one answered. Banqian stepped forward and said, "I have heard that in antiquity the star positions of Gu and Xu constituted the celestial formation;

sentences.zh: 山川向背，地陣也；

translations.literal: the facing of mountains and rivers formed the earth formation;
translations.idiomatic: the facing of mountains and rivers constituted the earth formation;

sentences.zh: 偏伍彌縫，人陣也。

translations.literal: and deploying partial ranks to bridge gaps formed the human formation.
translations.idiomatic: and deploying partial ranks to bridge gaps constituted the human formation.

sentences.zh: 臣謂不然。

translations.literal: I say this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I say that is not so.

sentences.zh: 夫師以義出，沛若時雨，得天之時，為天陣；

translations.literal: When an army sets out on righteous grounds, abundant as timely rain, seizing heaven's season — that is the celestial formation;
translations.idiomatic: When an army sets out on righteous grounds, abundant as timely rain, seizing heaven's season — that is the celestial formation;

sentences.zh: 足食約費，且耕且戰，得地之利，為地陣；

translations.literal: with ample food and restrained expenditure, tilling while fighting, gaining the land's advantage — that is the earth formation;
translations.idiomatic: with ample provisions and restrained expenditure, tilling while fighting, gaining the land's advantage — that is the earth formation;

sentences.zh: 舉三軍士如子弟從父兄，得人之和，為人陣。

translations.literal: treating the three armies' soldiers like sons and younger brothers following fathers and elder brothers, gaining human harmony — that is the human formation.
translations.idiomatic: treating the soldiers of the three armies like sons and younger brothers following fathers and elder brothers, gaining human harmony — that is the human formation.

sentences.zh: 舍是，則何以戰？」

translations.literal: Without these, upon what could one fight?
translations.idiomatic: Without these, upon what basis could one fight?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 既對策，擢高第。

translations.literal: After answering, he was promoted with top honors.
translations.idiomatic: After he finished his answers, he was placed at the top of the list.

sentences.zh: 歷華原、武功尉。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Huayuan and Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Huayuan and Wugong.

sentences.zh: 厭卑劇，求為左衛胄曹參軍。

translations.literal: Weary of low and arduous posts, he requested appointment as Army Staff Officer of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Weary of low and arduous posts, he requested appointment as army staff officer of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 使吐蕃，將行，武后曰：「久聞爾名，謂為古人，乃在朝邪！

translations.literal: When he was dispatched to Tibet, just before departure Empress Wu said: "I have long heard your name and thought you a man of antiquity — yet you are still in court!
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be sent as envoy to Tibet, Empress Wu said, "I have long heard your name and thought you a man of antiquity — yet you are still in court!

sentences.zh: 境外事不足行，宜留侍制。」

translations.literal: Affairs beyond the borders need not be undertaken; you should remain as attendant draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs beyond the borders need not trouble you; you should remain as attendant draftsman."

sentences.zh: 即詔入閤供奉。

translations.literal: Immediately he was ordered to enter the privy chamber in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Immediately he was ordered to enter the privy chamber to serve in attendance.

sentences.zh: 遷司賓寺主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 稍與丘悅、王劇、石抱忠同為弘文館直學士，又與路敬淳分日待制顯福門下。

translations.literal: Gradually he served with Qiu Yue, Wang Ju, and Shi Baozhong as regular academicians of the Hongwen Institute, and with Lu Jingchun took turns as attendant draftsman beneath Xianfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served with Qiu Yue, Wang Ju, and Shi Baozhong as regular academicians of the Hongwen Institute, and with Lu Jingchun took turns as attendant draftsman beneath Xianfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 擢累正諫大夫，兼右控鶴內供奉。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrating Grandee and concurrently Right Internal Attendant of the Crane Controllers.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to right remonstrating grandee and concurrently right internal attendant of the Crane Controllers.

sentences.zh: 半千以控鶴在古無有，而授任者皆浮狹少年，非朝廷德選，請罷之，忤旨，下遷水部郎中。

translations.literal: Banqian observed that controlling cranes had no precedent in antiquity and those appointed were all frivolous young men — not men chosen for virtue by the court; he petitioned to abolish it, defied the imperial will, and was demoted to Director of the Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Banqian held that the Crane Controllers had no precedent in antiquity and that those appointed were all frivolous young men — not men chosen for virtue by the court. He petitioned to abolish the office, defied the imperial will, and was demoted to director of the Water Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會詔擇牧守，除棣州刺史。

translations.literal: When an edict was issued to select prefects, he was appointed Prefect of Di.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was issued to select prefects and magistrates, he was appointed prefect of Di.

sentences.zh: 復入弘文館為學士。

translations.literal: He reentered the Hongwen Institute as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He reentered the Hongwen Institute as an academician.

sentences.zh: 武三思用事，以賢見忌，出豪、蘄二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wu Sansi held power, envied for his talent he was sent out as prefect of Hao and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sansi held power, envied for his talent he was sent out as prefect of Hao and Qi.

sentences.zh: 半千不丐任吏，常以文雅粉澤，故所至禮化大行。

translations.literal: Banqian did not petition for appointments; he always refined governance with literary grace, so wherever he went ritual and transformation flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Banqian did not petition for appointments; he always refined governance with literary culture, so wherever he went ritual and moral transformation flourished.

sentences.zh: 睿宗初，召為太子右諭德，仍學士職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ruizong's reign he was recalled as Right Mentor to the Crown Prince, retaining his academician duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ruizong's reign he was recalled as right mentor to the crown prince, retaining his duties as academician.

sentences.zh: 累封平原郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ennobled as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ennobled as Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 表丐骸骨，有詔聽朝朔望。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting retirement; an edict permitted him to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting retirement; an edict permitted him to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 半千事五君，有清白節，年老不衰，樂山水自放。

translations.literal: Banqian served five rulers, maintained an unsullied integrity, and though old did not decline, delighting to release himself among mountains and streams.
translations.idiomatic: Banqian served five rulers, maintained unsullied integrity, and though old did not flag, delighting to give himself over to mountains and streams.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，遊堯山、沮水間，愛其地，遂定居。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan he traveled between Mount Yao and the Ju River, loved the place, and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan he traveled between Mount Yao and the Ju River, fell in love with the country, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十四，即葬焉。

translations.literal: He died, aged ninety-four, and was buried there.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-four and was buried on the spot.

sentences.zh: 吏民哭野中。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners wept in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common people wept in the open countryside.

sentences.zh: 石抱忠

translations.literal: Shi Baozhong
translations.idiomatic: Shi Baozhong

sentences.zh: 抱忠，長安人。

translations.literal: Baozhong was a man of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong was a native of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 名屬文。

translations.literal: His given name was Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: His given name was Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 初置右臺，自清道率府長史為殿中侍御史，進檢校天官郎中，與侍郎劉奇、張詢古共領選，寡廉潔，而奇號清平，二人坐綦連耀伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Right Censorate was first established, he rose from Senior Administrator of the Qingdao Guard to Palace Censor, then advanced to Acting Director in the Ministry of Personnel. Together with Vice Ministers Liu Qi and Zhang Xungu he oversaw official selection. He was lacking in integrity, whereas Qi was known as upright and fair; both men were implicated with Qi Lianyao and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Right Censorate was first established, he was promoted from Senior Administrator of the Qingdao Guard to Palace Censor, and then to Acting Director in the Ministry of Personnel. He shared charge of official appointments with Vice Ministers Liu Qi and Zhang Xungu. Baozhong was corrupt, though Qi had a reputation for fairness; both were caught up in Qi Lianyao's conspiracy and put to death.

sentences.zh: 悅，河南人。

translations.literal: Yue was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 亦善論撰，仕至岐王傅。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at discourse and composition, and served until Tutor to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was also accomplished in expository writing, and rose to the post of Tutor to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 韓思彥

translations.literal: Han Siyan
translations.idiomatic: Han Siyan

sentences.zh: 韓思彥，字英遠，鄧州南陽人。

translations.literal: Han Siyan, courtesy name Yingyuan, was a man of Nanyang in Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Siyan, styled Yingyuan, was a native of Nanyang in Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遊太學，事博士谷那律。

translations.literal: He studied at the Imperial Academy under the Erudite Gu Naliu.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled in the Imperial Academy and studied under the Erudite Gu Naliu.

sentences.zh: 律為匪人所辱，思彥欲殺之，律不可。

translations.literal: When Naliu was insulted by a villain, Siyan wished to kill the man, but Naliu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruffian humiliated Naliu, Siyan wanted to kill him, but Naliu forbade it.

sentences.zh: 萬年令李乾祐異其才，舉下筆成章、誌烈秋霜科，擢第。

translations.literal: Li Qianyou, magistrate of Wannian, was struck by his talent and recommended him for the Compose Upon Writing and Steadfast as Autumn Frost examination categories; he passed and was selected.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianyou, magistrate of Wannian, recognized his gifts and nominated him for the Compose Upon Writing and Steadfast as Autumn Frost categories of the special examinations; Siyan passed and received his degree.

sentences.zh: 授監察御史，昌言當世得失。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor and spoke forthrightly on the gains and losses of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Censor and spoke bluntly about the strengths and failings of the times.

sentences.zh: 高宗夜召，加二階，待詔弘文館，伏內供奉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong summoned him at night, added two ranks, made him an attendant at the Hongwen Academy, and assigned him to inner palace service.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong summoned him after dark, promoted him two ranks, made him a Hanlin attendant at the Hongwen Academy, and posted him to confidential service within the palace.

sentences.zh: 巡察劍南，益州高貲兄弟相訟，累年不決，思彥敕廚宰飲以乳。

translations.literal: On an inspection tour of Jiannan, in Yizhou the brothers Gao Zi had been suing each other for years without resolution; Siyan ordered the kitchen staff to give them milk to drink.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Jiannan, he found that in Yizhou the brothers Gao Zi had been litigating against each other for years without end. Siyan ordered the kitchen to serve them milk.

sentences.zh: 二人寤，嚙肩相泣曰：「吾乃夷獠，不識孝義，公將以兄弟共乳而生邪！」

translations.literal: When the two came to their senses, they wept and bit each other's shoulders, saying, "We are barbarian tribesmen and did not understand filial piety and righteousness. Did you, sir, mean to remind us that brothers are born of the same mother's milk?"
translations.idiomatic: When the two men recovered, they wept and clutched each other's shoulders, saying, "We are frontier tribesmen who never learned filial duty or righteousness. Were you, sir, telling us that brothers share the milk of one mother?"

sentences.zh: 乃請輟訟。

translations.literal: They then asked to drop the lawsuit.
translations.idiomatic: They then asked to withdraw their suit.

sentences.zh: 至西洱河，誘叛蠻降之。

translations.literal: Reaching the West Er River, he persuaded rebellious barbarians to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the West Er River he persuaded rebel tribes to submit.

sentences.zh: 會蜀大饑，開倉振民，然後以聞，璽書褒美。

translations.literal: When Shu suffered a great famine, he opened the granaries to relieve the people and only then reported it; an imperial commendation praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was struck by severe famine, he opened the storehouses to feed the people and reported the matter afterward; the throne answered with a letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 使并州，方賊殺人，主名不立，醉胡懷刀而汙，訊掠已服。

translations.literal: Sent to Bingzhou: a murder had just occurred and the culprit was unknown; a drunken Hu man was found with a knife and bloodstains, and under interrogation and torture had already confessed.
translations.idiomatic: On assignment in Bingzhou, a murder had just been committed and the killer was unknown. A drunken Hu tribesman was found carrying a bloody knife; under torture he had already confessed.

sentences.zh: 思彥疑之，晨集童兒數百，暮出之，如是者三。

translations.literal: Siyan was suspicious. Each morning he gathered several hundred children, and each evening released them; he did this three times.
translations.idiomatic: Siyan had doubts. For three days running he assembled several hundred children in the morning and sent them out again at dusk.

sentences.zh: 因問：「兒出，亦有問者乎？」

translations.literal: He then asked, "When the children went out, was there anyone who questioned them?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "When the children left, did anyone question them?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「有之。」

translations.literal: All said, "There was."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "Yes, there was."

sentences.zh: 乃物色推訊，遂擒真盜。

translations.literal: He then tracked down suspects and interrogated them, and captured the real thief.
translations.idiomatic: He then identified and interrogated the suspects and seized the true culprit.

sentences.zh: 後太后晝見，勸帝修德答天譴。

translations.literal: Later the Empress Dowager received an audience in daylight and urged the emperor to cultivate virtue in answer to heaven's warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Wu held a daytime audience and urged the emperor to cultivate virtue to answer heaven's rebukes.

sentences.zh: 帝讓中書令李義府曰：「八品官能言得失，而卿冒沒富貴，主何事邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Chief Minister Li Yifu, saying, "An eighth-rank official can speak of gains and losses, yet you, immersed in wealth and rank—what affairs do you manage?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor upbraided Chief Minister Li Yifu: "A lowly eighth-rank official can speak plainly of right and wrong, yet you, drowning in wealth and status—what business are you actually tending?"

sentences.zh: 義府謝罪。

translations.literal: Yifu apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 司農武惟良擅用并州賦二百萬緡，思彥劾處死，武后為請而免。

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Wu Weiliang had misappropriated two million strings of Bingzhou tax revenue; Siyan impeached him for execution, but Empress Wu interceded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weiliang, Minister of Agriculture, had diverted two million strings of Bingzhou tax revenue; Siyan memorialized for his execution, but Empress Wu pleaded on his behalf and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 義府與諸武共譖思彥，出為山陽丞。

translations.literal: Yifu and the Wu clan jointly slandered Siyan, and he was sent out as Assistant Magistrate of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu and the Wu clan conspired to slander Siyan, and he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 初，尉遲敬德子姓陷大逆，思彥按釋其冤，至是贈黃金良馬，思彥不受。

translations.literal: Earlier, a clansman of Yuchi Jingde had been implicated in treason; Siyan investigated and cleared the injustice. Now they sent gifts of gold and fine horses, but Siyan would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, a kinsman of Yuchi Jingde had been caught up in a treason case; Siyan reviewed the file and cleared the man's name. Now they sent him gold and fine horses in gratitude, but Siyan refused.

sentences.zh: 至官閱月，自免去，放跡江、淮間。

translations.literal: After a month in office he resigned of his own accord and wandered between the Yangtze and Huai rivers.
translations.idiomatic: After only a month in post he resigned on his own and drifted along the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 久之，補建州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Registrar of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was appointed Registrar of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝召問：「不見卿久，今何官邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him and asked, "I have not seen you in a long while—what office do you hold now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and asked, "I have not seen you for ages—what post do you hold now?"

sentences.zh: 思彥泣道所以然。

translations.literal: Siyan wept and explained how matters had come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Siyan wept as he told the whole story.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰相：「此亦太屈。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chancellor, "This is too great an injustice."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the chief minister, "This is far too harsh."

sentences.zh: 復召為御史。

translations.literal: He summoned Siyan back as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Siyan and reappointed him as censor.

sentences.zh: 俄出為江都主簿，又徙蘇州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Secretary of Jiangdu, then transferred to Recording Secretary of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as Secretary of Jiangdu, then moved to Recording Secretary of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 罷，客汴州。

translations.literal: When dismissed, he stayed as a guest in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he lived as a guest in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張僧徹者，廬墓三十年，詔表其閭，請思彥為頌，餉縑二百，不受。

translations.literal: Zhang Sengche had kept vigil at his parents' tomb for thirty years; an edict honored his village, and he asked Siyan to compose a eulogy and offered two hundred bolts of silk, but Siyan would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sengche had kept mourning at his parents' grave for thirty years; the throne ordered his neighborhood honored, and he asked Siyan to write the commemorative text, offering two hundred bolts of silk—but Siyan declined.

sentences.zh: 時歲凶，家窶甚，僧徹固請，為受一匹，命其家曰：「此孝子縑，不可輕用。」

translations.literal: Times were famine-stricken and his household was very poor; Sengche pressed him insistently, so he accepted one bolt and told his family, "This is the filial son's silk—it must not be used lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Famine had left his household desperately poor; Sengche pressed him again and again, so he accepted a single bolt and told his family, "This silk comes from a filial son—it must not be spent carelessly."

sentences.zh: 上元中，復召見。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan reign he was summoned once more.

sentences.zh: 思彥久去朝，儀矩梗野，拜忘蹈舞，又詆外戚擅權，後惡之。

translations.literal: Siyan had long been away from court; his bearing was stiff and rustic, and he forgot the steps of the obeisance dance. He also denounced the empress's kin for monopolizing power, and she came to dislike him.
translations.idiomatic: Long absent from court, Siyan's manners had turned rough and unpolished; he forgot the ritual dance of obeisance. He also attacked the empress's relatives for seizing power, and she grew to resent him.

sentences.zh: 中書令李敬玄劾奏思彥見天子不蹈舞，負氣鞅鞅，不可用。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Jingxuan memorialized that Siyan, on seeing the Son of Heaven, did not perform the obeisance dance, bore resentment, and was unfit for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Jingxuan impeached Siyan for failing to perform the obeisance dance before the emperor, for nursing grievances, and for being unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 時已拜乾封丞，故徙朱鳶丞。

translations.literal: He had already been appointed Assistant Magistrate of Qianfeng, so he was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Zhuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been named Assistant Magistrate of Qianfeng, so instead he was reassigned to Assistant Magistrate of Zhuyuan.

sentences.zh: 遷賀州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretary of He Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretary of He Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 始，思彥在蜀，引什邡令鄧惲右坐，曰：「公且貴，願以子孫諉公。」

translations.literal: At the outset, when Siyan was in Shu, he seated Magistrate of Shifang Deng Yun in the seat of honor and said, "Sir, you will yet rise high; I wish to entrust my descendants to you."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Siyan was in Shu, he gave Magistrate Deng Yun of Shifang the seat of honor and said, "You are destined for high rank; I would like to commit my sons to your care."

sentences.zh: 比其斥，而惲已為文昌左丞。

translations.literal: By the time he was dismissed, Deng was already Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Siyan fell from favor, Deng had already become Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子琬。

translations.literal: His son Wan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan.

sentences.zh: 琬字茂貞，喜交酒徒，落魄少崖檢。

translations.literal: Wan, courtesy name Maozhen, delighted in the company of drinking companions and was unrestrained, with little sense of decorum.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, styled Maozhen, loved the company of carousing friends and lived in careless disarray, with scant regard for propriety.

sentences.zh: 有姻勸舉茂才，名動里中。

translations.literal: A relative by marriage urged him to enter the Maocai examination, and his name stirred the whole neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman by marriage urged him to sit for the Maocai examination, and his name soon rang through the district.

sentences.zh: 刺史行鄉飲餞之，主人揚觶曰：「孝於家，忠於國，今始充賦，請行無算爵。」

translations.literal: The prefect, on the village feast for sending off candidates, raised the horn cup and said, "Filial at home, loyal to the state—now taking the examination for the first time; please drink without counting the cups."
translations.idiomatic: At the district farewell feast the prefect raised the horn cup and said, "Filial at home, loyal to the throne—today you go to take the examination for the first time; drink, and let no one count the cups."

sentences.zh: 儒林榮之。

translations.literal: The literati honored this.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars present applauded the moment.

sentences.zh: 擢第，又舉文藝優長、賢良方正，連中。

translations.literal: He passed the examination, and also passed the Outstanding Literary Talent and Worthy and Upright categories in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination, then passed the Outstanding Literary Talent and Worthy and Upright categories one after another.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，上言：

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingyun era he submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingyun era he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 國安危在於政。

translations.literal: The safety or peril of the state lies in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state stands or falls depends on how it is governed.

sentences.zh: 政以法，暫安焉必危；

translations.literal: When governance relies on law, though temporarily secure, it must eventually become perilous;
translations.idiomatic: Govern by law alone, and though the realm may seem secure for a time, danger is sure to follow;

sentences.zh: 以德，始不便焉終治。

translations.literal: when it relies on virtue, though at first inconvenient, ultimately there is good order.
translations.idiomatic: govern by virtue, and though the start may be awkward, lasting order will come in the end.

sentences.zh: 夫法者，智也；

translations.literal: Law is cunning;
translations.idiomatic: Law is cleverness;

sentences.zh: 德者，道也。

translations.literal: virtue is the Way.
translations.idiomatic: virtue is the Way.

sentences.zh: 智，權宜也；

translations.literal: Cunning is expedience;
translations.idiomatic: Cleverness is a temporary expedient;

sentences.zh: 道，可以久大也。

translations.literal: the Way can endure and expand.
translations.idiomatic: the Way is what can endure and grow great.

sentences.zh: 故以智治國，國之賊；

translations.literal: Thus to govern the state with cunning is to be the state's villain;
translations.idiomatic: To rule a state by cleverness is to become the state's enemy;

sentences.zh: 不以智治國，國之福。

translations.literal: not to govern the state with cunning is the state's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: to refuse to rule by cleverness is the state's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、永徽之間，農不勸而耕者眾，法施而犯者寡；

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, farmers needed no urging yet many plowed; when law was applied, violators were few;
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan and Yonghui reigns, farmers needed no prodding yet the fields were full; laws were in force, yet offenders were rare;

sentences.zh: 俗不偷薄，器不行窳；

translations.literal: customs were not grasping or shallow, and vessels were not shoddy;
translations.idiomatic: morals were neither greedy nor mean, and goods were not made flimsy;

sentences.zh: 吏貪者士恥同列，忠正清白者比肩而立；

translations.literal: greedy officials were shamed by gentlemen of the same rank, and loyal, upright, pure officials stood shoulder to shoulder;
translations.idiomatic: officials who took bribes were ashamed before their peers, while the loyal, upright, and incorrupt stood side by side;

sentences.zh: 罰雖輕而不犯，賞雖薄而勸；

translations.literal: punishments though light were not violated, and rewards though meager still encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: punishments were light, yet no one broke the law; rewards were small, yet people still strove for them;

sentences.zh: 位尊不倨，家富不奢；

translations.literal: those of high rank were not arrogant, and wealthy families were not extravagant;
translations.idiomatic: the high-born were not haughty, and rich households were not wasteful;

sentences.zh: 學校不勵而勤，道佛不懲而戒；

translations.literal: schools needed no prodding yet students were diligent, and Daoism and Buddhism needed no punishment yet people were restrained;
translations.idiomatic: schools needed no special urging yet students applied themselves; Daoist and Buddhist clergy needed no crackdown yet people kept their discipline;

sentences.zh: 土木質厚，裨販弗蚩。

translations.literal: builders and craftsmen were solid in quality, and petty traders were not deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: builders and artisans worked in earnest, and street peddlers did not cheat their customers.

sentences.zh: 其故奈何？

translations.literal: Why was this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why was this so?

sentences.zh: 維以皇道也。

translations.literal: Because of the sovereign's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Because the throne ruled by the supreme Way.

sentences.zh: 自茲以來，任巧智，斥謇諤；

translations.literal: Since then, cunning has been employed and blunt honest speech rejected;
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, cleverness has been prized and plainspoken honesty driven out;

sentences.zh: 趨勢者進，守道者退；

translations.literal: those who chase trends advance, and those who hold to the Way retreat;
translations.idiomatic: men who follow the tide rise, while men who keep to the Way fall back;

sentences.zh: 諧附者無黜剝之憂，正直者有後時之嘆；

translations.literal: those who harmonize and fawn have no fear of dismissal, while the upright have sighs of being passed over;
translations.idiomatic: flatterers need never fear demotion, while the honest are left sighing in the rear;

sentences.zh: 人趨家競，風俗淪替。

translations.literal: people rush and families compete, and customs have degenerated.
translations.idiomatic: every man scrambles, every household contends, and the manners of the age have collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其故奈何？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 行以霸道也。

translations.literal: Because rule by hegemonic force is practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Because the throne now rules by brute expedience.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、永徽之天下，亦今日天下，淳薄相反，由治則然。

translations.literal: The empire of Zhenguan and Yonghui is the same empire as today; purity and decadence are opposite—such is the result of good governance versus bad.
translations.idiomatic: The realm of Zhenguan and Yonghui is the same realm we have today; that it was once pure and is now corrupt comes of nothing but the difference between good government and bad.

sentences.zh: 夫巧者知忠孝為立身之階，仁義為百行之本，托以求進，口是而心非，言同而意乖，陛下安能盡察哉！

translations.literal: The cunning know that filial piety and loyalty are steps to advancement and that benevolence and righteousness are the root of all conduct; they employ these to seek promotion—mouth yes but heart no, words agree but intent diverges—how can Your Majesty fully discern this!
translations.idiomatic: The clever know that filial piety and loyalty are ladders to promotion, and that benevolence and righteousness are the foundation of every virtue—they invoke them to advance, yes on the lips but no in the heart, agreement in words but treachery in intent. How can Your Majesty see through them all!

sentences.zh: 貪冒者謂能，清貞者謂孤，浮沈者為黠，剛正者為愚。

translations.literal: The greedy and corrupt are called capable; the pure and upright are called isolated; the slick are called clever; the firm and upright are called foolish.
translations.idiomatic: The grasping are praised as able; the clean-handed are mocked as aloof; the smooth are hailed as sharp; the steadfast are dismissed as dull.

sentences.zh: 位下而驕，家貧而奢。

translations.literal: Low in rank yet arrogant; poor in household yet extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Men of low rank act insolent; households in poverty live in luxury.

sentences.zh: 歲月漸漬，不救其弊，何由變浮之淳哉？

translations.literal: If months and years gradually soak in without remedying these ills, how can the superficial be transformed back to purity?
translations.idiomatic: If year after year these faults are left to deepen unchecked, how will the age ever turn from shallow display back to genuine integrity?

sentences.zh: 不務省事而務捉搦。

translations.literal: Not striving to streamline governance but striving to catch and prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: The court does not seek to simplify administration—it seeks only to hunt down offenders.

sentences.zh: 夫捉搦者，法也。

translations.literal: Catching and prosecuting is law.
translations.idiomatic: That hunting down of offenders is what law has become.

sentences.zh: 法設而滋章，滋章則盜賊多矣。

translations.literal: When law is established it grows ever more elaborate; when ever more elaborate, thieves and bandits multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Once laws are set in place they only grow more tangled; the more tangled they become, the more thieves and rogues there are.

sentences.zh: 法而益國，設之可也。

translations.literal: If law benefits the state, then it may be established.
translations.idiomatic: When laws truly benefit the realm, they may rightly be instituted.

sentences.zh: 比法令數改，或行未見益，止未知損。

translations.literal: Recently laws and orders have been changed repeatedly; sometimes when put into practice no benefit is seen, and when stopped no harm is known.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes have been revised again and again of late—often with no visible gain when enacted, and no clear loss when abandoned.

sentences.zh: 譬弈者一棋為善，而復之者愈善，故曰設法不如息事，事息則巧不生。

translations.literal: It is like players of weiqi: one move may be good, yet those who repeat and multiply moves deem themselves even better. Hence the saying that establishing laws is not as good as settling affairs; when affairs are settled, craftiness does not arise.
translations.idiomatic: It is like go: one good move may suffice, yet some players multiply their moves thinking more is better—hence the adage that legislating pales beside quieting disputes; when affairs are settled, cunning finds no opening.

sentences.zh: 聖人防亂未然，天下何繇不治哉？

translations.literal: The sage guards against disorder before it arises—how could the realm not be well governed?
translations.idiomatic: The sage wards off chaos before it takes shape; under such governance, how could the realm fail to prosper?

sentences.zh: 永淳時，雍丘令尹元貞坐婦女治道免官，今婦夫女役常不知怪。

translations.literal: During the Yongchun era, Yongqiu magistrate Yin Yuanzhen was dismissed from office for having women maintain the roads; today women being conscripted for corvée labor is commonly regarded without surprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongchun period, Yongqiu magistrate Yin Yuanzhen was removed for employing women on road repair—a scandal then, but today no one blinks at wives and daughters pressed into labor service.

sentences.zh: 調露時，河內尉劉憲父喪，人有請其員者，有司以為名教不取，今謂為見機。

translations.literal: During the Diaolu era, Henei Commandant Liu Xian was in mourning for his father, and when someone requested his vacant post the authorities deemed it contrary to the norms of teaching and rejected it; today such conduct is called seizing the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, when Henei Commandant Liu Xian mourned his father and someone sought his vacant post, the authorities refused on grounds of propriety—whereas today the same opportunism is praised as shrewd foresight.

sentences.zh: 太宗朝，司農以市木橦倍價抵罪，大理孫伏伽言：「官木橦貴，故百姓者賤。

translations.literal: In the Taizong reign, the Minister of Agriculture was convicted for selling tung timber at double the price. Sun Fugai of the Court of Judicial Review said: "Official tung timber is expensive, so the common people sell cheaply.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taizong's day, the Minister of Agriculture was charged with selling government tung timber at double price. Sun Fugai of the Court of Judicial Review argued: "State timber was overpriced, forcing the people to sell cheaply.

sentences.zh: 臣見司農識大體，未聞其過。」

translations.literal: Your subject sees that the Minister of Agriculture understood the larger pattern and has not heard of his fault."
translations.idiomatic: In my view the Minister grasped the broader situation; I see no fault in his conduct."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 今和市專刻剝，名為和而實奪之。

translations.literal: Today government market purchases are devoted to harsh exploitation, called harmonization while in fact seizing goods.
translations.idiomatic: Today state procurement systematically gouges merchants—called "fair exchange" while in truth stripping them bare.

sentences.zh: 往者學生、佐史、里正每一員闕，擬者十人，今當選者亡匿以免。

translations.literal: Formerly, for each vacancy among students, clerks, and village heads, ten candidates were proposed; today those selected hide and flee to avoid service.
translations.idiomatic: Once, ten men competed for every opening among students, clerks, and village heads; now appointees go into hiding to escape duty.

sentences.zh: 往選司從容有禮，今如仇敵賈販。

translations.literal: Formerly the selection office was leisurely and courteous; today it is like hostile merchants haggling.
translations.idiomatic: Selection offices once treated candidates with courtesy; now they bargain like bitter merchant rivals.

sentences.zh: 往官將代，儲什物俟其至；

translations.literal: Formerly when an official was about to be replaced, stores of goods were kept awaiting his arrival;
translations.idiomatic: Incoming officials once found supplies stocked and waiting for their arrival;

sentences.zh: 今交罷，執符紛競校在亡。

translations.literal: today at handover of office, tally slips are grasped and contested in chaotic reckoning of what is missing.
translations.idiomatic: now at handover they fight over tally slips in frantic accounting of what has vanished.

sentences.zh: 往商賈出入萬里，今市井至失業。

translations.literal: Formerly merchants traveled tens of thousands of li; today market towns reach the point of unemployment.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants once ranged freely across vast distances; now market towns see widespread unemployment.

sentences.zh: 往家藏鏹積粟相匏，今匿貲示羸以相尚。

translations.literal: Formerly households hoarded cash and piled grain like gourds; today they conceal wealth and display destitution as a point of pride.
translations.idiomatic: Families once openly hoarded coin and grain; now they hide assets and feign poverty as a virtue.

sentences.zh: 往夷狄款關，今軍屯積年。

translations.literal: Formerly the barbarians came offering allegiance at the passes; today garrisons stand for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians once came offering tribute at the borders; now armies camp year after year.

sentences.zh: 往召募，人賈其勇；

translations.literal: Formerly in recruitment, men prized their courage;
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment once drew volunteers proud of their valor;

sentences.zh: 今差勒，闔宗逃亡。

translations.literal: today under forced levy, whole clans flee.
translations.idiomatic: now under conscription entire clans take flight.

sentences.zh: 往倉儲盈衍，今所在空虛。

translations.literal: Formerly granaries overflowed; today everywhere stands empty.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries once overflowed; now storehouses everywhere stand empty.

sentences.zh: 夫流亡之人非愛羈旅、忘桑梓也，斂重役亟，家產已空，鄰伍牽連，遂為遊人。

translations.literal: Exiles do not love being bound to travel or forget their native place; taxes are heavy and corvée urgent, household property is already exhausted, neighbors are implicated, and thus they become wanderers.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees do not love wandering or forget their homelands—heavy levies and urgent corvée drain them dry, neighboring households are dragged in, and they become rootless wanderers.

sentences.zh: 窮詐而犯禁，救死而抵刑。

translations.literal: Driven to the utmost of deception they violate prohibitions; struggling to save their lives they incur punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Driven to deception by desperation, they break the law; struggling to survive, they face punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫亂繩已結，急引之則不可解。

translations.literal: When a tangled rope is already knotted, pulling it urgently cannot be undone.
translations.idiomatic: Once a rope is tangled into knots, yanking at it only makes it worse.

sentences.zh: 今刻薄吏能結者也，舉劾吏能引者也，則解者不見其人。

translations.literal: Today harsh officials are those who can tie knots, and impeaching officials are those who can pull; then those who can untie are nowhere seen.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh officials tighten the knot, investigating officials yank at it—and no one remains who can unravel the mess.

sentences.zh: 願取奇材卓行者，量能授官。

translations.literal: I wish that men of extraordinary talent and outstanding conduct be selected and offices granted according to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that men of exceptional talent and upright conduct be chosen and given office according to their capacity.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He further stated:
translations.idiomatic: He further stated:

sentences.zh: 仕路太廣，故棄農商而趨之。

translations.literal: The paths to office are too broad, so people abandon farming and commerce to rush toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Too many routes lead to office, so people abandon farming and trade to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 一夫耕，一婦蠶，衣食百人，欲儲蓄有餘，安可得乎？

translations.literal: One man plows and one woman raises silkworms to clothe and feed a hundred people—wishing to have surplus in storage, how can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: One man farms and one woman raises silkworms to feed and clothe a hundred mouths—how could they hope to save anything?

sentences.zh: 書入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 出監河北軍，兼按察使。

translations.literal: He went out to oversee the Hebei armies, concurrently serving as surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to oversee the Hebei armies while also serving as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先天中，賦絹非時，於是谷賤縑益貴，丁別二縑，人多徙亡。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era, silk tribute was levied out of season; thus grain was cheap while silk grew dearer, and each adult male owed two bolts of silk—many people fled.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian period, silk levies were demanded off schedule; grain prices collapsed while silk soared, and each adult male owed two bolts—driving masses to flee.

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「御史乃耳目官，知而不言，尚何賴？」

translations.literal: Wan said: "Censors are the eyes and ears of the throne; if they know and do not speak, what is there to rely on?
translations.idiomatic: Wan said: "Censors are the emperor's eyes and ears—if we know and stay silent, what good are we?"

sentences.zh: 又上言：「須報則弊已甚，移檄罷督乃聞。」

translations.literal: He further submitted: "If one must wait for a report, the harm will already be severe; only after dispatching an edict to halt the levy supervisor was it heard."
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned again, "If we must wait for approval, the damage will already be severe; only by sending an edict to halt the levy supervisor can it be heard in time."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 開元中，遷殿中侍御史，坐事貶官，卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was promoted to palace censor, was demoted for an offense, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan period he was promoted to palace censor, later demoted for an offense, and died.

sentences.zh: 蘇安恒

translations.literal: Su Anheng
translations.idiomatic: Su Anheng

sentences.zh: 蘇安恒，冀州武邑人。

translations.literal: Su Anheng was a native of Wuyi in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Anheng came from Wuyi in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 博學，尤明《周官》、《春秋左氏》學。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned, especially expert in the learning of the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned, with particular mastery of the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 武后末年，太子雖還東宮，政事一不與，大臣畏禍無敢言。

translations.literal: In the late years of Empress Wu, although the crown prince had returned to the Eastern Palace, he was given no part in state affairs; the great ministers feared disaster and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's final years, though the crown prince had returned to the Eastern Palace, he was excluded from all affairs of state, and no minister dared speak for fear of disaster.

sentences.zh: 安恒投匭上書曰：「陛下膺先聖顧托，受嗣子揖讓，應天順人，二十餘年，豈不聞虞舜褰裳、周公復辟事乎？

translations.literal: Anheng submitted a memorial through the suggestion box, saying: "Your Majesty received the dying charge of the former sages, accepted the abdication of the heir, and responded to Heaven and accorded with the people for more than twenty years—have you not heard of how Yu Shun lifted his robe and the Duke of Zhou restored the throne?
translations.idiomatic: Anheng dropped a memorial into the suggestion box: "Your Majesty received the former emperors' dying charge, accepted the crown prince's abdication, and has ruled fitly for more than twenty years—have you forgotten how Shun yielded the throne and the Duke of Zhou restored it?

sentences.zh: 今太子孝謹，春秋盛壯，使統臨宸極，何異陛下身撫天下哉！

translations.literal: Now the crown prince is filial and prudent, in the prime of life; to have him preside over the imperial seat—how does it differ from Your Majesty personally governing the realm!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is filial, prudent, and in the prime of life—if he ascended the throne, would that differ from Your Majesty governing in person?

sentences.zh: 胡不傳位東宮，休安聖躬？

translations.literal: Why not transfer the throne to the Eastern Palace and rest and settle the sacred person?
translations.idiomatic: Why not transfer power to the Eastern Palace and allow yourself rest and ease?

sentences.zh: 自昔天下無二姓並興，且梁、河內、建昌諸王，以親得封，恐萬歲後不能良計，宜退就公侯，任以閑簡。

translations.literal: From antiquity two surnames have never risen together under Heaven; moreover the princes of Liang, Hennei, and Jianchang received fiefs through kinship—I fear that after Your Majesty's passing they cannot be well managed; they should step back to the ranks of duke and marquis and be assigned idle posts.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity no two surnames have risen together; the princes of Liang, Hennei, and Jianchang hold titles through kinship—when you pass, they may prove unmanageable. They should step back to lesser noble ranks and be given quiet appointments.

sentences.zh: 又陛下二十孫，無尺土封，非長久計也，請以都督府要州分而王之。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty's twenty grandsons hold not a foot of territory—this is no long-term plan; I ask that key prefectures of the area commands be divided and enfeoffed to them as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your twenty grandsons hold not a foot of territory—a poor long-term strategy. Grant them frontier prefectures as princely domains.

sentences.zh: 縱今尚幼，且擇立師傅，養成德器，藩屏皇家。」

translations.literal: Even if they are still young, tutors should be chosen and established to cultivate their virtue and capacity, as bulwarks of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Though still young, choose tutors to cultivate their virtue and make them bulwarks of the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 書奏，後雖猜克，不能無感，乃召見賜食，厚慰遣之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Empress though suspicious could not be without feeling; she summoned him, bestowed food, comforted him generously, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Empress Wu remained suspicious but was moved; she summoned him, offered a meal, comforted him generously, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 明年，復諫曰：「臣聞天下者，高祖、太宗之天下。

translations.literal: The next year he remonstrated again, saying: "Your subject has heard that the realm is the realm of Gaozu and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he remonstrated again: "The realm belongs to Gaozu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 有隋失馭，群雄鹿駭，唐家親事戎旅，以平宇縣，指河為誓，非李氏不王，非功臣不封。

translations.literal: Sui lost control of the reins; lords contended like stags in alarm. The Tang house personally took up arms to pacify the realm, swearing by the Yellow River that none but the Li clan would be kings and none but meritorious ministers would receive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui lost control, lords contended like frightened stags. The Tang personally took up arms to pacify the realm, swearing by the Yellow River that none but the Li clan would rule and none but meritorious ministers receive fiefs.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖居正統，實唐舊基。

translations.literal: Your Majesty though occupying the orthodox succession in fact stands on the old foundation of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty holds legitimate succession, you stand on the Tang dynasty's foundation.

sentences.zh: 日前太子在諒暗，相王非長嗣，唐祚中弱，故陛下因以即位。

translations.literal: Previously the crown prince was in mourning, the Prince of Xiang was not the eldest heir, and the Tang fortune was weakened in mid-course—thus Your Majesty accordingly ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was in mourning and the Prince of Xiang was not the eldest heir, the Tang line was weakened—hence Your Majesty took the throne.

sentences.zh: 今太子年德已盛，尚貪有大寶，忘母子之恩，蔽其元良，以據神器，何旅顏面見唐家宗廟、大帝陵寢哉！

translations.literal: Now the crown prince's years and virtue are already flourishing, yet you still covet the great treasure, forget the bond between mother and son, obscure the rightful heir, and occupy the sacred regalia—how can you show your face before the Tang ancestral temple and the late emperor's tomb!
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince has reached maturity in years and virtue, yet you cling to supreme power, forget the bond between mother and son, block your rightful heir from the sacred regalia—how can you face the Tang ancestral temple and the late emperor's tomb with any composure!

sentences.zh: 臣謂天意人事，還歸李氏。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that Heaven's intent and human affairs alike return to the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Heaven and human affairs alike demanded the return of rule to the Li clan.

sentences.zh: 物極則復，器滿則覆；

translations.literal: When things reach their limit they turn back; when a vessel is full it overturns;
translations.idiomatic: When things reach their limit they reverse; when a vessel fills it overturns;

sentences.zh: 當斷不斷，將受其亂。

translations.literal: when one should cut but does not, one will suffer the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: hesitation at the decisive moment invites chaos.

sentences.zh: 誠能高揖萬機，自怡聖心，史臣書之，樂府歌之，斯盛事也。

translations.literal: If you can truly yield the myriad affairs of state high above and settle your sacred heart in contentment, historians will record it and the Music Bureau will sing of it—this would be a grand event.
translations.idiomatic: If you could relinquish affairs of state and cultivate serenity, historians would record it and court musicians celebrate—a truly splendid achievement.

sentences.zh: 臣聞見過不諫非忠，畏死不言非勇。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that to see fault and not remonstrate is not loyalty; to fear death and not speak is not courage.
translations.idiomatic: To see fault and not remonstrate is disloyalty; to fear death and stay silent is cowardice.

sentences.zh: 陛下以臣為忠，則擇是而用；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds your subject loyal, then choose this and employ it;
translations.idiomatic: If you deem me loyal, heed my counsel;

sentences.zh: 以為不忠，則斬臣頭以令天下。」

translations.literal: if you hold me disloyal, then cut off my head to command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: if disloyal, behead me as an example to the realm."

sentences.zh: 書聞，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was heard, no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 於是魏元忠為張易之克弟所構，獄方急，安恒獨申救曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei Yuanzhong was framed by the younger brother of Zhang Yizhi; the case was urgent, and Anheng alone pleaded for his rescue, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yuanzhong was framed by Zhang Yizhi's younger brother and faced imminent trial, Anheng alone spoke in his defense:

sentences.zh: 王者有容天下之量，故濟其心；

translations.literal: A king has the measure to accommodate all under Heaven, and thus comforts their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: A true ruler possesses the magnanimity to accommodate all under Heaven and thereby comfort their hearts;

sentences.zh: 能進天下之善，故除其惡。

translations.literal: he can advance the good of all under Heaven, and thus removes their evil.
translations.idiomatic: he promotes goodness throughout the realm and thereby removes evil.

sentences.zh: 不然，則神鬼馮怒，陰陽紛舛。

translations.literal: Otherwise, then gods and spirits grow wrathful and yin and yang fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise gods and spirits grow wrathful and yin and yang fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 陛下始革命，勤秉政樞，博逮謀猷，天下以為明主。

translations.literal: Your Majesty at the beginning of the revolution diligently held the reins of government, broadly reaching for plans and counsel—the realm regarded you as an enlightened ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At the revolution's outset you diligently held the reins, sought counsel broadly, and the realm hailed an enlightened sovereign.

sentences.zh: 暮年厭怠，讒佞熾結，水火相災，百姓不親，五品不遜，天下以為暗君。

translations.literal: In your declining years you grew weary and slack; slanderers and flatterers flourished and entwined; fire and water brought mutual calamity; the people were not close; the five ranks were not deferential—the realm regarded you as a dark ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In your declining years, weariness and sycophants took hold, calamities multiplied, the people grew estranged, ranks lost deference, and the realm saw a darkened ruler.

sentences.zh: 邪正糅進，獄訟冤劇。

translations.literal: The wicked and the upright were mixed together; lawsuits and imprisonments were grievously unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil mingled indiscriminately; lawsuits overflowed with injustice.

sentences.zh: 何昔是而今非邪？

translations.literal: Why was it right then and wrong now?
translations.idiomatic: How had right become wrong?

sentences.zh: 居安忘危之失也。

translations.literal: It is the fault of finding ease and forgetting peril.
translations.idiomatic: It was the failure of finding ease and forgetting peril.

sentences.zh: 竊見元忠廉直有名，位宰相，履忠正，邪佞之徒嫉之若讎。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that Yuanzhong is upright and famous; he holds the rank of chancellor and treads the path of loyalty and rectitude—the wicked and flatterers hate him as they would an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was renowned for integrity, served as chancellor with upright conduct, and was hated as a mortal enemy by the wicked.

sentences.zh: 易之兄弟無功無德，但以馮附，不閱數期，位勢隆極，指馬獻蒲，先害善良。

translations.literal: The brothers Yizhi had no merit and no virtue; they relied only on fawning attachment, and within a few periods their rank and power reached the utmost—they pointed at a horse and offered a rush, first harming the good and worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang brothers possessed neither merit nor virtue yet rose to supreme power through flattery alone within a few years, twisting truth and destroying the good.

sentences.zh: 自元忠下獄，人人偶語，謂易之交亂，且及四國。

translations.literal: Since Yuanzhong was cast into prison, everyone whispered in pairs, saying that Yizhi's faction would bring disorder and even reach the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanzhong's imprisonment, people whispered that Zhang Yizhi's faction would bring rebellion affecting the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 烈士撫髀，忠臣鉗口，懼易之之權，恐先諫受戮，虛死無名。

translations.literal: Men of fierce resolve beat their thighs; loyal ministers sealed their mouths, fearing Yizhi's power, dreading that those who remonstrated first would be executed—dying in vain without fame.
