translations.idiomatic: Men of valor beat their thighs in frustration while loyal ministers sealed their lips, fearing Zhang's power and knowing early remonstrance meant death without honor.

sentences.zh: 況賊虜方強，賦斂重困，而自縱讒慝，搖變遐邇。

translations.literal: Moreover the enemy barbarians are just then strong, and tax levies heavily afflict the people—yet you yourself indulge slander and wickedness, stirring change near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover external enemies grow strong while heavy taxes oppress the people, yet you indulge slanderers, stirring unrest near and far.

sentences.zh: 臣恐四夷低目窺覘，為邊鄙患，百姓托義以清君側，逐鹿之人叩關而至，陛衛左右，從中以應，爭鋒朱雀之門，問鼎大明之宮，陛下何以謝之？

translations.literal: Your subject fears that the four barbarians will lower their eyes to peep and watch, becoming a border affliction; the people will take righteous cause to purge the ruler's side; those contending for the deer will knock at the passes and arrive; guards left and right will respond from within; they will clash at the Gate of the Vermilion Bird and contend for the cauldron at the Palace of Great Brightness—how will Your Majesty answer them?
translations.idiomatic: I fear foreign peoples will watch with lowered eyes and become border threats; subjects may rally under righteous banners to purge the court; rival claimants will storm the gates while traitors within open the palace—how will you answer when battle erupts at Zhuque Gate and usurpers seek the throne at Daming Palace?

sentences.zh: 臣今計者，莫若收雷電之威，解恢恢之網，復爵還位，君臣如初，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your subject's plan now is none other than to gather the might of thunder and lightning, loosen the vast net, restore ranks and return to office, and let ruler and ministers be as at first—then the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel is to wield your full authority, loosen the net of punishment, restore ranks and office, and let ruler and ministers be as before—the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不能斬佞臣，塞人望，且當抑奪榮寵，翦其羽翅，無使驕橫為社稷之憂。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty cannot execute the flatterers and block the people's hopes, you should at least suppress and strip their honors and glory, cut their wings, and not let their arrogance become a worry for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you cannot execute the sycophants and satisfy public expectation, at minimum strip their honors and clip their wings before their arrogance endangers the state.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，易之等大怒，遣刺客邀殺之，賴鳳閣舍人桓彥範等悉力營解，乃免。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yizhi and the others were greatly enraged and sent assassins to intercept and kill him; thanks to Palace Aide Huan Yanfan and others exerting all their strength to rescue and explain, he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Zhang brothers furiously sent assassins to kill him, but Palace Aide Huan Yanfan and others worked strenuously to save him.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為習藝館內教。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he served as instructor within the Training Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he served as instructor in the Training Hall.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子難，或讒安恒豫謀，死獄中。

translations.literal: At the crisis of Crown Prince Jiemin, some slandered Anheng as having plotted beforehand, and he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Jiemin's tragedy, slanderers accused Anheng of complicity, and he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，知其枉，詔贈諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, knowing he had been wronged, he issued an edict posthumously granting him Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, recognizing his innocence, he posthumously granted him Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 薛登，常州義興人。

translations.literal: Xue Deng was a native of Yixing in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Deng came from Yixing in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父士通，為隋鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: His father Shitong served as a yingyang langjiang of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shitong served as a Sui yingyang langjiang.

sentences.zh: 江都亂，與州民聞人遂安據城拒賊。

translations.literal: At the Jiangdu uprising, together with the prefectural people he joined Minren Suian in holding the city to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiangdu uprising, he joined the local people and Minren Suian in holding the city against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 武德初，持地自歸，授東武州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era he submitted his territory and returned to allegiance, and was appointed governor of Dongwu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wude period he submitted to Tang and was appointed governor of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏反，士通與賊將西門君儀戰，破之。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, Shitong fought the rebel general Ximen Junyi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, Shitong fought rebel general Ximen Junyi and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 及平，封臨汾侯。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 終泉州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as governor of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as governor of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 登通貫文史，善議論，根證該審，與徐堅、劉子玄齊名。

translations.literal: Deng was thoroughly versed in literature and history, skilled in disputation, with roots and evidence comprehensive and careful; he was famed alongside Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Deng was thoroughly versed in literature and history, skilled in debate with meticulous evidence, and ranked alongside Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 調閬中主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 天授中，累遷左補闕。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era, he was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou period, he rose through successive appointments to Left Assistant Censor.

sentences.zh: 時選舉濫甚，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time recommendations for office were extremely indiscriminate, so he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time official recommendations had become grossly indiscriminate, and he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 比觀舉薦，類不以才，馳聲假譽，互相推引，非所謂報國求賢者也。

translations.literal: Recently observing recommendations, they generally do not select by talent; people spread reputations with false praise and recommend one another—these are not what is meant by serving the state and seeking worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Of late I have observed that recommendations rarely rest on talent. Men broadcast their names with borrowed reputations and promote one another in turn. This is not what is meant by serving the state and seeking the worthy.

sentences.zh: 古之取士，考素行之原，詢鄉邑之譽，崇禮讓，明節義，以敦樸為先，雕文為後。

translations.literal: In antiquity when selecting scholars, they examined the origin of plain conduct, inquired into the reputation of the home district, honored ritual deference, clarified integrity and duty, putting plainness first and ornate writing last.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when selecting men for office, rulers examined the roots of plain conduct and inquired into a candidate's standing in his home district. They honored ritual deference and made integrity clear, putting solid character first and polished writing second.

sentences.zh: 故人崇勸讓，士去輕浮，以計貢賢愚為州之榮辱。

translations.literal: Therefore people esteemed encouragement and deference, scholars discarded frivolity, and whether the tribute recommendation counted wise or foolish was the glory or shame of a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, people valued mutual encouragement and yielding, scholars cast off frivolity, and whether a prefecture's tribute recommendations were wise or foolish became a matter of local honor or disgrace.

sentences.zh: 昔李陵降而隴西溯，幹木隱而西河美。

translations.literal: Formerly when Li Ling surrendered, Longxi turned away; when Gan Mu lived in seclusion, Xihe was honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Li Ling surrendered, Longxi turned away in shame; when Gan Mu lived in seclusion, Xihe was held up as a model.

sentences.zh: 名勝於利，則偷競日銷；

translations.literal: When fame exceeds profit, then stealthy rivalry daily diminishes;
translations.idiomatic: When fame outweighs profit, underhand rivalry daily fades;

sentences.zh: 利勝於名，則貪暴滋煽。

translations.literal: When profit exceeds fame, then greed and violence increasingly flare.
translations.idiomatic: when profit outweighs fame, greed and violence grow ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 蓋冀缺以禮讓升而晉人知禮，文翁以經術教而蜀士多儒。

translations.literal: For Ji Que rose through ritual deference and the people of Jin knew ritual; Wen Weng taught through classical learning and the scholars of Shu were mostly Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Que rose through ritual deference, and the people of Jin learned propriety; Wen Weng taught the classics, and the scholars of Shu became largely Confucian.

sentences.zh: 未有上好而下不從者也。

translations.literal: Never has the ruler above valued something and those below not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has a ruler above set the standard and those below failed to follow.

sentences.zh: 漢世求士，必觀其行，故士有自脩，為閭里推舉，然後府寺交辟。

translations.literal: In Han times when seeking scholars, conduct was always observed; thus scholars cultivated themselves, were recommended by their neighborhoods, and only then did government offices jointly recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, when seeking men for office the court always looked to conduct. Scholars cultivated themselves, were recommended by their neighborhoods, and only then were they recruited by one government office after another.

sentences.zh: 魏取放達，晉先門閥，梁、陳薦士特尚詞賦。

translations.literal: Wei took those of free and unrestrained talent; Jin prioritized clan status; Liang and Chen especially favored literary composition in recommending scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Wei favored men of free and unrestrained talent; Jin put clan status first; and under Liang and Chen, recommendations chiefly prized literary composition.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝納李諤之言，詔禁文章浮詞，時泗州刺史司馬幼之表不典實得罪，由是風俗稍改。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Li E's advice and issued an edict prohibiting inflated language in essays; at the time the prefect of Si Prefecture Sima Youzhi submitted a memorial that was not solid in fact and was punished; from this customs gradually changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Li E's counsel and issued an edict forbidding inflated phrasing in essays. At the time Sima Youzhi, prefect of Si Prefecture, submitted a memorial lacking solid substance and was punished for it, and from that point customs began to change.

sentences.zh: 煬帝始置進士等科，後生復相馳競，赴速趨時，緝綴小文，名曰策學，不指實為本，而以浮虛為貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang first established the jinshi examinations and other categories; later generations again competed with one another, rushing to keep pace with the times, stitching together minor essays called 'examination learning,' not taking solid achievement as the foundation but valuing empty show.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang first established the jinshi degree and related categories, and later generations again raced one another, hurrying to keep up with the times, patching together minor essays in what was called examination learning. Solid achievement was no longer the foundation; empty display was what counted.

sentences.zh: 方今舉士，尤乖其本。

translations.literal: Today in selecting scholars, this departs especially from the root.
translations.idiomatic: Today's selection of scholars departs from that root more than ever.

sentences.zh: 明昭方下，固已驅馳府寺之廷，出入王公之第，陳篇希恩，奏記誓報。

translations.literal: As soon as the edict of clear announcement is issued, candidates already rush to the halls of government offices, enter and leave the mansions of princes and dukes, presenting essays hoping for favor, submitting petitions vowing repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly has the edict of announcement been issued when candidates are already racing through the halls of government offices and in and out of princes' and dukes' mansions, presenting essays in hope of favor and submitting petitions vowing repayment.

sentences.zh: 故俗號舉人皆稱覓舉。

translations.literal: Therefore by custom examination candidates are all called those 'seeking recommendation.'
translations.idiomatic: For this reason candidates are popularly called those who 'seek recommendation.'

sentences.zh: 覓者，自求也，非彼知之義。

translations.literal: 'Seeking' means seeking on one's own—not the meaning of 'the other knowing.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Seeking' means seeking on one's own—it is not the sense of being discovered by others.

sentences.zh: 是以耿介之士羞於自拔，循常小人棄疏取附。

translations.literal: Therefore upright men are ashamed to promote themselves, while ordinary petty men abandon those who are distant and attach to those close.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, upright men are ashamed to promote themselves, while ordinary petty men abandon the distant and attach themselves to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 願陛下降明制，頒峻科，斷無當之遊言，收實用之良策，文試效官，武閱守禦。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would issue clear regulations, promulgate strict standards, cut off irrelevant idle talk, collect practical good policies, test literary candidates by actual performance in office, and examine military candidates by guarding and defending.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty issue clear regulations and promulgate strict standards, cut off irrelevant chatter, and gather policies of real use: test literary candidates by their performance in office, and military candidates by their ability to guard and defend.

sentences.zh: 昔吳起將戰，左右進劍，吳子辭之，諸葛亮臨陣，不親戎服，蓋不取弓劍之用也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Wu Qi was about to do battle, his attendants presented swords; Master Wu declined them. Zhuge Liang at the battle line did not personally wear military dress—generally they did not rely on bow and sword.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Wu Qi was about to give battle, his attendants offered swords and Master Wu declined them. Zhuge Liang at the front did not himself don military dress. In both cases they did not rely on bow and blade.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝聞司馬相如之文，恨不與同時，及其至也，終不處以公卿之位，非所任故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han heard of Sima Xiangru's writing and regretted not being contemporary with him; yet when he arrived, he was never placed in a grand minister's position—for that was not what he was fit for.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han heard of Sima Xiangru's writings and regretted that they were not contemporaries. Yet when Xiangru arrived at court, he was never given a grand minister's post, because that was not what he was fit for.

sentences.zh: 漢法，所舉之主，終身保任。

translations.literal: Han law: the recommender bears lifelong guarantee for those he recommends.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, the man who recommended an appointee bore lifelong responsibility for him.

sentences.zh: 楊雄之坐田儀，成子之得魏相，賞罰之令行，則請謁之心絕；

translations.literal: Yang Xiong being implicated because of Tian Yi, Chengzi obtaining Wei Xiang—as when reward and punishment are enforced, the heart of petitioning dies;
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xiong was implicated because of Tian Yi, and when Chengzi obtained Wei Xiang as minister—once the commands of reward and punishment are enforced, the urge to petition dies;

sentences.zh: 退讓之義著，則貪競之路銷。

translations.literal: When the meaning of yielding is displayed, the path of greedy rivalry is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: when the principle of yielding is made clear, the road of greedy rivalry is cut off.

sentences.zh: 請寬年限，以容簡汰，不實免官，得人加賞，自然見賢不隱，貪祿不專矣。

translations.literal: Please extend the term so that selection and elimination may be accommodated: if the recommendation proves untrue, dismiss from office; if a worthy man is obtained, add reward—in this way naturally the worthy will be seen and not hidden, and those grasping for salary will not monopolize.
translations.idiomatic: Please extend the term of accountability so that selection and elimination have room to work: if a recommendation proves false, remove the man from office; if a worthy man is found, add reward. Then naturally the worthy will not be hidden and those grasping for salary will not monopolize office.

sentences.zh: 時四夷質子多在京師，如論欽陵、阿史德元珍、孫萬榮，皆因入侍見中國法度，及還，並為邊害。

translations.literal: At the time many hostages from the four barbarians were in the capital, such as Lun Qinling, Ashide Yuanzhen, and Sun Wanrong—all because through attending court they saw China's laws and institutions, and upon returning, each became a border harm.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many hostages from the four directions were in the capital, men such as Lun Qinling, Ashide Yuanzhen, and Sun Wanrong. Each had learned China's laws and institutions while attending court, and upon returning home each became a scourge on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 登諫曰：

translations.literal: Deng remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Deng remonstrated, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞戎、夏不雜，古所戒也。

translations.literal: Your minister hears that barbarian and Chinese should not be mixed—this is an ancient warning.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister has heard that barbarians and Chinese should not be mixed—this is a warning handed down from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 故斥居塞外，有時朝謁，已事則歸，三王之法也。

translations.literal: Therefore they were kept outside the frontier, coming to court at times and returning when business was done—this was the law of the Three Sage Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they were kept beyond the frontier, coming to court only at set times and returning once their business was done. That was the law of the Three Sage Kings.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，革襲衣冠，築室京師，不令歸國。

translations.literal: Since Han and Wei, they have changed to wear Chinese dress, built houses in the capital, and are not allowed to return to their states.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, the practice has changed: hostages adopt Chinese dress, build houses in the capital, and are not permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 較其利害，三王是而漢、魏非，拒邊長而質子短。

translations.literal: Comparing the benefits and harms: the Three Kings were right and Han-Wei wrong; keeping them at the frontier is long-term while hostages is short-term.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the benefits and harms: the Three Kings were right and Han and Wei wrong. Keeping barbarians at the frontier is a long-term policy; keeping hostages is a short-term one.

sentences.zh: 昔晉郭欽、江統以夷狄處中夏必為變，武帝不納，卒有永嘉之亂。

translations.literal: Formerly in Jin, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong held that placing barbarians in central China would surely lead to rebellion; Emperor Wu did not accept this, and ultimately there was the Yongjia disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong argued that settling barbarians in the heartland of China would surely lead to upheaval. Emperor Wu did not accept their counsel, and in the end came the Yongjia disaster.

sentences.zh: 伏見突厥、吐蕃、契丹往因入侍，並被獎遇，官戎秩，步黌門，服改氈罽，語習楚夏，窺圖史成敗，熟山川險易。

translations.literal: Humbly observing: Turks, Tibetans, and Khitans in the past because of attending court were all rewarded and favored—given military ranks, walking through the school gates, changing dress to felt and wool, learning both barbarian and Chinese speech, peering at maps and histories for success and failure, becoming familiar with the terrain and strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Turks, Tibetans, and Khitans who in the past attended court were all rewarded and favored: given military rank, admitted to the schools, changing their dress for felt and wool, learning both barbarian and Chinese speech, studying maps and histories for lessons of success and failure, and becoming familiar with the terrain and its strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 國家雖有冠帶之名，而狼子孤恩，患必在後。

translations.literal: Though the state gives them the name of cap and belt, they are wolf's cubs who forget kindness—disaster is sure to come later.
translations.idiomatic: Though the state gives them the name of civilized subjects, they are wolf cubs who forget kindness. Disaster is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 昔申公奔晉，使子狐庸為吳行人，教吳戰陣，使之叛楚。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Shen fled to Jin and sent Zihu Yong as Wu's envoy, teaching Wu battle formations, causing Wu to rebel against Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Duke Shen fled to Jin and sent Zihu Yong as Wu's envoy, teaching Wu battle formations and turning Wu against Chu.

sentences.zh: 漢遷五部匈奴於汾、晉，卒以劉、石作難。

translations.literal: Han relocated the five Xiongnu divisions to Fen and Jin, and ultimately Liu and Shi raised trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Han relocated the five Xiongnu divisions to the Fen and Jin region, and in the end Liu Yuan and Shi Le raised rebellion.

sentences.zh: 竊計秦並天下，及劉、項用兵，人士雕散，以冒頓之盛，乘中國之虛，而高祖困厄平城，匈奴卒不入中國者，以其生長磧漠，謂穹廬賢於城郭，氈罽美於章紱，既安所習，是以無窺中國心，不樂漢故也。

translations.literal: I consider: when Qin united the empire and when Liu and Xiang Yu fought, scholars and people were scattered; though Modu was at his height and took advantage of China's emptiness, and though Gaozu was distressed at Pingcheng, the Xiongnu ultimately did not enter China because they grew up in the desert, considered yurts superior to walled cities, felt felt and wool more beautiful than official ribbons—they were content with what they were used to, and therefore had no heart to look covetously at China and did not enjoy Han customs.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon that when Qin united the empire and Liu Bang and Xiang Yu fought, the people were scattered. Though Modu was at the height of his power and seized on China's weakness, and though Gaozu was hard pressed at Pingcheng, the Xiongnu in the end did not enter China because they had grown up in the desert. They thought yurts better than walled cities and felt and wool finer than official insignia. Content with what they knew, they had no heart to covet China and took no pleasure in Han ways.

sentences.zh: 元海五部散亡之餘而能自振者，少居內地，明習漢法，鄙單于之陋，竊帝王之稱。

translations.literal: Among the scattered remnant of the five divisions, Liu Yuan was able to revive himself because from youth he lived in the interior, clearly knew Han law, despised the Single Chanyu's rustic ways, and usurped the title of emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, among the scattered remnant of the five divisions, was able to revive himself because from youth he lived in the interior, knew Han law well, despised the Chanyu's rustic ways, and usurped the title of emperor.

sentences.zh: 使其未嘗內徙，不過劫邊人繒彩、曲糵歸陰山而已。

translations.literal: If he had never been moved inward, he would have done no more than raid border people for silk and ale and return to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Had he never been moved inland, he would have done no more than raid border people for silk and ale and return to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 今皇風所覃，含識革面，方由余效忠，日磾盡節。

translations.literal: Now the imperial wind extends everywhere, all conscious beings change their faces; just as You Yu showed loyalty and Jin Midi showed utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial influence reaches everywhere and all who have understanding change their ways, as You Yu showed loyalty and Jin Midi showed utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 然臣慮備豫不謹，則夷狄稱兵不在方外，非貽謀之道。

translations.literal: Yet your minister worries that if precautions are not careful, barbarians raising arms will not stay beyond the frontier—this is not the way to leave counsel for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that if precautions are not taken with care, barbarians who take up arms will not remain beyond the frontier. That is not the way to leave sound counsel for posterity.

sentences.zh: 臣謂願充侍子可一切禁絕，先在國者不使歸蕃，則夷人保疆，邊邑無爭。

translations.literal: Your minister holds that those sent as attending sons should all be completely prohibited; those already in China should not be allowed to return to their tribes—then barbarians will keep their borders and frontier towns will be without strife.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister holds that sending hostages to attend at court should be completely forbidden, and those already in the realm should not be allowed to return to their tribes. Then the barbarians will keep to their borders and the frontier towns will be free of strife.

sentences.zh: 武后不納。

translations.literal: Empress Wu did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time, he went out as prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬宣州賊鐘大眼亂，百姓潰震，登嚴勒守備，闔境賴安。

translations.literal: When the bandit Zhong Dayan rebelled in Xuan Prefecture, the people were shaken and dispersed; Deng strictly enforced defenses and the whole jurisdiction relied on him for safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Zhong Dayan rebelled in Xuanzhou, the people were shaken and scattered. Deng strictly enforced defenses, and the whole prefecture owed its safety to him.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，為御史大夫。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era, he became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun period he served as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 僧慧範怙太平公主勢，奪民邸肆，官不能直，登將治之，或勸以自安，答曰：「憲府直枉，朝奏暮黜可矣。」

translations.literal: The monk Huifan relied on Princess Taiping's power, seized common people's shops—the government could not set things right. When Deng was about to punish him, someone urged self-preservation; he replied: 'The censorate sets wrongs right—memorialize in the morning and dismiss by evening, that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huifan relied on Princess Taiping's power and seized shops from common people, and the authorities could not set matters right. When Deng was about to prosecute him, someone urged him to protect himself. He replied, 'The censorate exists to set wrongs right. A memorial in the morning and dismissal by evening will suffice."

sentences.zh: 遂劾奏，反為主所構，出岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He then submitted an impeachment but was instead framed by the princess and sent out as prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted an impeachment, but was instead framed by the princess and sent out as prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Advisor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Advisor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為東都留守，再為太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he was Eastern Capital Intendant; again served as Advisor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he served as Eastern Capital Intendant, and later again as Advisor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 登本名謙光，以與皇太子名同，詔賜今名。

translations.literal: Deng's original name was Qianguang; because it was the same as the crown prince's name, an edict gave him his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's original name was Qianguang. Because it was identical to the crown prince's name, an edict granted him his present name.

sentences.zh: 坐子累歸田里，家苦貧，詔給致仕祿。

translations.literal: Because of his son's offense he returned to the countryside; his family was deeply poor and an edict granted him retired salary.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his son's offense he returned to the countryside. His family was deeply poor, and an edict granted him a retired official's stipend.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-three; posthumously awarded prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three and was posthumously awarded the title of prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 王求禮

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli

sentences.zh: 王求禮，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli was a native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli was a native of Changshe in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 武后時，為左拾遺、監察御史。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time, he was Left Reminder and Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign he served as Left Reminder and Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 後方營明堂，雕飾譎怪，侈而不法。

translations.literal: The Empress was building the Bright Hall with carved ornamentation, strange and bizarre, extravagant and not according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was then building the Bright Hall, ornamented with strange and bizarre carvings, extravagant and contrary to proper standards.

sentences.zh: 求禮以為「鐵鸑金龍、丹雘珠玉，乃商瓊臺、夏瑤室之比，非古所謂茅茨棌椽者。

translations.literal: Qiuli held that 'iron phoenixes, golden dragons, cinnabar lacquer and pearls and jade are comparable to Shang's Qiongtai and Xia's Yaoshi—not what antiquity called thatched roofs and rafters of oak.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli held, "Iron phoenixes, golden dragons, cinnabar lacquer, pearls, and jade are on a par with Shang's Jade Tower and Xia's Jasper Hall—not what antiquity meant by thatched roofs and rafters of oak.

sentences.zh: 自軒轅以來，服牛乘馬，今輦以人負，則人代畜」，上書譏切。

translations.literal: 'Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, people rode oxen and horses; now the carriage is borne by men—then men replace beasts.' He submitted a memorial with sharp sarcasm.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, men have ridden oxen and horses. Now the imperial carriage is borne by men—men have taken the place of beasts." He submitted a memorial with biting sarcasm.

sentences.zh: 久不報。

translations.literal: For a long time there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time there was no response.

sentences.zh: 契丹叛，使孫萬榮寇河北，詔河內王武懿宗禦之，懦擾不進，賊敗數州去。

translations.literal: The Khitans rebelled and sent Sun Wanrong to raid Hebei; an edict ordered Wu Yizong, Prince of Hennei, to resist him—he was cowardly and agitated, not advancing, and the bandits defeated several prefectures and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans rebelled and sent Sun Wanrong to raid Hebei. An edict ordered Wu Yizong, Prince of Hennei, to resist him. He was cowardly and agitated and would not advance, and the rebels overran several prefectures before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 懿宗乃條華人為賊詿誤者數百族，請誅之。

translations.literal: Yizong then listed several hundred clans of Chinese whom the bandits had misled, requesting their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong then drew up a list of several hundred Chinese clans whom he claimed the rebels had misled, and requested that they be executed.

sentences.zh: 求禮劾奏曰：「詿誤之人無良邊吏教習，城不完固，為虜脅制，寧素持叛心哉？

translations.literal: Qiuli submitted an impeachment, saying: 'Those who were misled had no good frontier officials to instruct them; the walls were not complete and strong—they were compelled by the barbarians; how could they have long harbored rebellious hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli submitted an impeachment, saying, 'Those who were misled had no capable frontier officials to instruct them. The walls were not complete and strong, and they were compelled by the enemy. How could they have long harbored rebellious hearts?

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁兵數十萬，聞敵至，走保城邑，今乃移禍無辜之人，不亦過乎？

translations.literal: Yizong held an army of several hundred thousand; when he heard the enemy arrive he fled to walled cities—now he shifts calamity onto innocent people; is this not excessive?
translations.idiomatic: Yizong commanded an army of several hundred thousand men. When he heard the enemy was coming he fled to walled cities. Now he shifts the blame onto innocent people—is that not going too far?

sentences.zh: 請斬懿宗首以謝河北。」

translations.literal: I request that Yizong's head be cut off to appease Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yizong's head be cut off to appease Hebei."

sentences.zh: 懿宗大懼，後盡赦其人。

translations.literal: Yizong was greatly terrified; the Empress fully pardoned those people.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong was greatly terrified, and the Empress fully pardoned those people.

sentences.zh: 當是時，契丹陷幽州，饋免屈竭，左相豆盧欽望請停京官九品以上兩月奉助軍興。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitans took Youzhou; supply transport was exhausted; Left Chancellor Doulu Qinwang requested stopping two months' salary for capital officials of the ninth rank and above to aid military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitans had taken Youzhou, supply lines were exhausted, and Left Chancellor Doulu Qinwang requested that capital officials of the ninth rank and above forgo two months' salary to aid military expenses.

sentences.zh: 求禮曰：「公祿萬鐘，正可輟，仰祿之人可奈何？」

translations.literal: Qiuli said: 'Those with salary of ten thousand piculs may properly forgo it—but what about those who depend on salary?
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli said, 'Those who draw salaries of ten thousand piculs may properly forgo them—but what of those who live on their stipends?"

sentences.zh: 欽望拒不應。

translations.literal: Qinwang refused to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 既奏，求禮歷階進曰：「天子富有四海，何待九品奉，使宰相奪之以濟軍國用乎？」

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted, Qiuli mounted the steps and advanced saying: 'The Son of Heaven possesses the wealth of the four seas—why depend on ninth-rank salaries and have the chancellor seize them to aid military and state expenses?
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, Qiuli mounted the steps and advanced, saying, 'The Son of Heaven possesses the wealth of the four seas. Why must he rely on ninth-rank salaries and have the chancellor seize them to meet military and state expenses?"

sentences.zh: 姚璹曰：「秦、漢皆有稅算以佐軍，求禮不識大體。」

translations.literal: Yao Shu said: 'Qin and Han both had tax assessments to aid the army—Qiuli does not understand the larger picture.'
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shu said, 'Qin and Han both levied special taxes to aid the army. Qiuli does not understand the larger picture.'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「秦、漢虛天下事邊，奈何使陛下效之？」

translations.literal: He replied: 'Qin and Han exhausted the empire on frontier affairs—why have Your Majesty imitate them?'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'Qin and Han exhausted the empire on frontier affairs. Why should Your Majesty follow their example?'

sentences.zh: 後曰：「止。」

translations.literal: The Empress said: 'Stop.'
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, 'Enough.'

sentences.zh: 久視二年三月，大雨雪，鳳閣侍郎蘇味道等以為瑞，率群臣入賀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Jiushi, there was heavy rain and snow; Vice Minister Su Weidao and others took it as an auspicious sign and led the ministers in to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of the Jiushi era there was heavy rain and snow. Su Weidao, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, and others took it as an auspicious sign and led the ministers in to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 求禮讓曰：「宰相燮和陰陽，而季春雨雪，乃災也。

translations.literal: Qiuli objected, saying: 'The chancellor harmonizes yin and yang—yet spring snow in the third month is a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli objected, saying, 'The chancellor is charged with harmonizing yin and yang, yet snow in the third month of spring is a disaster.

sentences.zh: 果以為瑞，則冬月雷，渠為瑞雷邪？」

translations.literal: If you truly take this as auspicious, then thunder in winter—would that be auspicious thunder?
translations.idiomatic: If you truly take this as auspicious, then would thunder in winter be auspicious thunder as well?"

sentences.zh: 味道不從。

translations.literal: Weidao did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao would not agree.

sentences.zh: 既賀者入，求禮即厲言：「今陽氣僨升，而陰冰激射，此天災也。

translations.literal: When those coming to congratulate entered, Qiuli immediately spoke sharply: 'Now yang qi surges upward while yin ice shoots forth—this is a heavenly disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When those coming to congratulate entered, Qiuli immediately spoke sharply: 'Now yang qi surges upward while yin ice shoots forth. This is a heavenly disaster.

sentences.zh: 主荒臣佞，寒暑失序，戎狄亂華，盜賊繁興，正官少，偽官多，百司非賄不入，使天有瑞，何感而來哉？」

translations.literal: The ruler is negligent and ministers are flatterers; cold and heat are out of order; barbarians disturb China; bandits abound; proper officials are few, false officials many; every office admits none without bribes—if heaven had an auspicious sign, what would it respond to?
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is negligent and ministers are flatterers. Cold and heat are out of order, barbarians disturb China, and bandits abound. Proper officials are few and false officials many. No office admits anyone without a bribe. If heaven had an auspicious sign, what would it be responding to?"

sentences.zh: 群臣震恐，後為罷朝。

translations.literal: The ministers were shaken with fear; the Empress dismissed court because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were shaken with fear, and the Empress dismissed court because of it.

sentences.zh: 然以剛正故，宦齟齬。

translations.literal: Yet because of his firm uprightness, his official career was full of friction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of his firm uprightness, his official career was full of friction.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，終衛王府參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, he ended as staff member of the Prince of Wei's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he ended his career as a staff member in the household of the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 柳澤，蒲州解人。

translations.literal: Liu Ze was a native of Jie in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ze was a native of Jie in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖亨，字嘉禮，隋大業末，為王屋長，陷李密，已而歸京師。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Heng, courtesy name Jiali, at the end of Sui Daye era was magistrate of Wangwu; he fell into Li Mi's hands, then later returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Heng, courtesy name Jiali, at the end of the Daye era of Sui served as magistrate of Wangwu. He fell into Li Mi's hands, but later returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 姿貌魁異，高祖奇之，以外孫竇妻之。

translations.literal: His appearance was towering and extraordinary; Gaozu found him remarkable and gave him a granddaughter of the Dou clan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was towering and extraordinary. Gaozu found him remarkable and gave him a granddaughter of the Dou clan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 三遷左衛中郎將，壽陵縣男。

translations.literal: Three times he was transferred to Left Guard Commandant of the Center, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Shouling.
translations.idiomatic: After three successive appointments as Left Guard Commandant of the Center, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shouling.

sentences.zh: 以罪貶邛州刺史，進散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For a crime he was demoted to Prefect of Qiongzhou; he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Palace Aid.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to Prefect of Qiongzhou, but was later promoted to Regular Attendant of the Palace Aid.

sentences.zh: 代還，數年不得調。

translations.literal: When replaced and returned, for several years he received no reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: After his successor took over and he returned to the capital, he went several years without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 持兄喪，方葬，會太宗幸南山，因得召見，哀之。

translations.literal: Observing mourning for his elder brother, just as he was about to bury him, it happened that Emperor Taizong visited the Southern Mountains, and so he obtained a summons and audience; the emperor pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his elder brother and on the point of burying him, Emperor Taizong happened to be touring the Southern Mountains. Hen was summoned for an audience, and the emperor took pity on him.

sentences.zh: 數日，入對北門，拜光祿少卿。

translations.literal: After several days, he entered and answered at the North Gate, and was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Household Office.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was examined at the North Gate and appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Household Office.

sentences.zh: 亨射獵無檢，帝謂曰：「卿於朕舊且親，然多交遊，自今宜少戒。」

translations.literal: Heng hunted and shot without restraint. The emperor said to him: "You, sir, are both an old acquaintance and a kinsman of mine, yet you have many social connections—from today you should restrain yourself somewhat."
translations.idiomatic: Heng hunted without restraint. The emperor said to him, "You are both an old friend and a kinsman of mine, yet you keep too much company. From now on you should show some restraint."

sentences.zh: 亨由是痛飭厲，謝賓客，身安靜素，力吏事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Heng rigorously disciplined himself, dismissed guests, kept himself quiet and plain, and devoted his strength to official duties.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Heng took the admonition to heart, cut off his visitors, lived quietly and simply, and threw himself into his official responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 終檢校岐州刺史，贈禮部尚書、幽州都督，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He ultimately served as acting Inspector of Qizhou; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites and Area Commander of Youzhou; his posthumous epithet was Gong ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as acting prefect of Qizhou and, after death, was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites and area commander of Youzhou, with the posthumous epithet Respecting.

sentences.zh: 澤耿介少言笑，風度方嚴。

translations.literal: Ze was upright and uncompromising, rarely laughing or jesting; his bearing was upright and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ze was scrupulously upright and spoke little; his deportment was dignified and austere.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，為右率府鎧曹參軍，四歲不遷。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era he was Army Armor Officer of the Right Guard Office, and for four years received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun reign period (710–712) he served as army armor officer in the Right Guard Office and went four years without advancement.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗時，長寧、宜城、定安諸公主及後女弟、昭容上官與其母鄭、尚宮柴、隴西夫人趙及姻聯數十族，皆能降墨敕授官，號斜封。

translations.literal: Previously, during the time of Emperor Zhongzong, the Princesses of Changning, Yicheng, and Ding'an, the empress's younger sisters, the Brilliant Lady Shangguan and her mother Zheng, Lady Chai of the Inner Palace, Lady Zhao of Longxi, and dozens of families linked by marriage—all could have imperial edicts in black ink sent down to confer office; they were called "diagonal seal" appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Emperor Zhongzong, the Princesses of Changning, Yicheng, and Ding'an, the empress's younger sisters, Lady Shangguan the Brilliant Attendant and her mother Lady Zheng, Inner Palace Lady Chai, Longxi Lady Zhao, and dozens of allied families by marriage could all issue appointments through informal imperial edicts—the so-called "side-seal" offices.

sentences.zh: 及姚元崇、宋璟輔政，白罷斜封官數千員。

translations.literal: When Yao Yuanchong and Song Jing assisted in government, they reported and abolished several thousand side-seal offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Yuanchong and Song Jing took charge of the government, they had several thousand of these side-seal appointees dismissed on memorial.

sentences.zh: 元崇等罷去，太平公主盡奏復之。

translations.literal: When Yuanchong and the others were dismissed and departed, Princess Taiping memorialized to restore them all.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao and his colleagues were removed from office, Princess Taiping had all of them restored by memorial.

sentences.zh: 澤詣闕上疏曰：

translations.literal: Ze went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ze went to court and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞藥不毒不可以蠲疾，詞不切不可以補過。

translations.literal: I have heard that medicine that is not potent cannot dispel illness, and words that are not incisive cannot remedy faults.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that medicine without potency cannot cure disease, and words without sharpness cannot set right errors.

sentences.zh: 故習甘旨者，非攝養之方；

translations.literal: Therefore one accustomed to sweet flavors—this is not the method of nourishing the constitution;
translations.idiomatic: A diet of nothing but sweetness is no way to nourish the body;

sentences.zh: 邇諛佞者，非治安之宜。

translations.literal: drawing near to flatterers and sycophants—this is not what is suitable for governing and bringing peace.
translations.idiomatic: and consorting with flatterers and sycophants is no way to secure good government.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見神龍以來，綱紀大壞，內寵專命，外嬖制權，因貴憑勢，賣官鬻爵。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed that since the Shenlong era the norms and discipline have been greatly ruined: inner favorites monopolized appointments, outer paramours controlled power; relying on nobility and leaning on influence, they sold offices and peddled ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched, since the Shenlong era, how the moral order has collapsed utterly: palace favorites controlled appointments, outside favorites wielded power, and the well-born and well-connected trafficked in offices and sold noble titles.

sentences.zh: 妃主之門同商賈然，舉選之署若阛阓然，屠販者由邪忝官，廢黜者因奸冒進。

translations.literal: The gates of princesses were like those of merchants; the offices of selection were like market streets. Butchers and peddlers through crooked means occupied office in shame; the dismissed and deposed through deceit and imposture advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The doors of princesses became market stalls; the selection bureaus became bazaars. Butchers and hawkers bought their way into office by devious routes, while the dismissed and disgraced regained rank through fraud.

sentences.zh: 天下混亂，幾危社稷，賴陛下聰明神武，拯溺舉墜。

translations.literal: Under heaven there was chaos; the altars of grain and soil were nearly endangered. We rely on Your Majesty's intelligence, sagacity, and martial prowess—rescuing the drowning and lifting up what has fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The realm fell into turmoil and the dynasty itself was nearly lost. It is thanks to Your Majesty's intelligence and martial prowess that the drowning were pulled out and the fallen lifted up.

sentences.zh: 耳目所親，豈可忘鑒誡哉？

translations.literal: What one's eyes and ears have personally witnessed—how can one forget it as a mirror and warning?
translations.idiomatic: Having seen and heard these things with your own senses, how can you forget them as a lesson and a warning?

sentences.zh: 且斜封官者，皆仆妾私謁，迷謬先帝，豈盡先帝意邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, side-seal officers were all private petitions by male and female servants, misleading and confusing the late emperor—how could they fully represent the late emperor's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, side-seal appointments all came from private petitions by servants and concubines, misguiding the late emperor. Could they truly have reflected his will?

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之初，用元崇等計，悉以停廢，今又收用之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession, following the plan of Yuanchong and others, all were stopped and abolished; now they are again gathered and employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of your reign you followed Yao Yuanchong's counsel and abolished them all; now you have taken them back into service.

sentences.zh: 若斜封之人不可棄邪，韋月將、燕欽融不應褒贈，李多祚、鄭克義不容蕩雪也。

translations.literal: If side-seal persons cannot be abandoned, then Wei Yuejiang and Yan Qinrong ought not to be praised and rewarded; Li Duozhuo and Zheng Keyi cannot be allowed to be cleansed and cleared.
translations.idiomatic: If side-seal appointees are not to be cast off, then Wei Yuejiang and Yan Qinrong should not have been honored posthumously, and Li Duozhuo and Zheng Keyi should not have been pardoned and rehabilitated.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不能忍於此而能忍於彼，使善惡混並，反覆相攻，道人以非，勸人以僻。

translations.literal: Your Majesty—why can you not bear with this yet can bear with that? It makes good and evil mixed together, repeatedly attacking each other; showing people the wrong path, encouraging people in devious ways.
translations.idiomatic: Why can Your Majesty not tolerate the one but tolerate the other, mingling good with evil in a churn of reversal, teaching men what is wrong and encouraging them in crooked paths?

sentences.zh: 今天下咸稱太平公主與胡僧慧範以此誤陛下，故語曰：「姚、宋為相，邪不如正；

translations.literal: Now all under heaven alike say that Princess Taiping and the barbarian monk Huifan by this misled Your Majesty. Hence the saying: "When Yao and Song were chancellors, the crooked was not as good as the straight;
translations.idiomatic: All the realm now says Princess Taiping and the foreign monk Huifan misled Your Majesty in this matter. Hence the saying: "When Yao and Song were chancellors, wrong fell short of right;

sentences.zh: 太平用事，正不如邪。」

translations.literal: When Taiping held power, the straight was not as good as the crooked.
translations.idiomatic: when Taiping held power, right fell short of wrong."

sentences.zh: 臣恐流遁致遠，積小為大，累微成高。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that what drifts and escapes will reach far; accumulating the small makes the large, amassing the minute makes the lofty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that what escapes notice in the moment may reach far, that small accumulations grow large and minute additions mount high.

sentences.zh: 勿謂何傷，其禍將長；

translations.literal: Do not say "What harm is there?"—the calamity will lengthen;
translations.idiomatic: Do not say "What harm can it do?"—for the calamity will lengthen;

sentences.zh: 勿謂何害，其禍將大。

translations.literal: Do not say "What damage is there?"—the calamity will grow great.
translations.idiomatic: and do not say "What damage can it do?"—for the calamity will grow great.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He further stated:
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say:

sentences.zh: 尚醫奉御彭君慶以巫覡小伎超授三品，奈何輕用名器，加非其人？

translations.literal: Palace Medical Attendant Peng Junqing, on account of minor witchcraft and shamanistic tricks, was abruptly granted third rank—how can one lightly use honored instruments of office and apply them to one who is not the right person?
translations.idiomatic: Palace Medical Attendant Peng Junqing was abruptly promoted to third rank on the strength of shamanistic tricks. How can you lightly bestow dignified offices on the wrong man?

sentences.zh: 臣聞賞一人而千萬人悅者，賞之；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: when rewarding one man makes ten million rejoice, reward him;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when rewarding one man will please ten thousand others, reward him;

sentences.zh: 罰一人而千萬人勸者，罰之。

translations.literal: when punishing one man makes ten million take warning, punish him.
translations.idiomatic: and when punishing one man will warn ten thousand others, punish him.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁察。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty judge and examine.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no reply was given.

sentences.zh: 澤入調，會有詔選者得言事。

translations.literal: When Ze entered for reassignment, it happened that there was an edict allowing those selected to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ze went up for reassignment, an edict happened to allow selected candidates to address the throne on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 乃上書曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 頃者韋氏蠱亂，奸臣同惡，政以賄成，官以寵進，言正者獲戾，行殊者見疑，海內寒心，人用不保。

translations.literal: Recently the Wei clan wrought sorcery and chaos; wicked ministers shared in the evil. Government was completed by bribes; office advanced through favor. Those who spoke rightly incurred blame; those whose conduct was extraordinary were viewed with suspicion. Within the seas hearts turned cold; men could not secure their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the Wei faction plunged the court into sorcerous turmoil, and corrupt ministers acted in concert. Offices were bought, posts were won through favor, straight talk brought punishment, and unusual conduct aroused suspicion. The whole realm grew fearful, and no one could feel secure.

sentences.zh: 陛下神聖勇智，安宗社於已危，振黎苗之將溺。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sacred, sage, courageous, and wise—securing the altars of grain and soil when already endangered, rousing the common multitudes when about to drown.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, sacred in wisdom and resolute in courage, saved the altars of state when they were already imperiled and lifted the people when they were near drowning.

sentences.zh: 乃今蠲煩省徭，法明德舉，萬邦愷樂，室家胥歡。

translations.literal: Thus now abolishing burdens and reducing corvée labor, clarifying virtue and exalting worth, the myriad regions are joyful, every household is together in gladness.
translations.idiomatic: You have now eased burdens and lightened corvée, made the law bright and promoted virtue. The myriad states rejoice, and every household shares in happiness.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says: "There is hardly anyone without a beginning; few can have an end.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "It is seldom indeed that anything is without a beginning; few things have a proper end."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下慎厥初，脩其終。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty be careful of its beginning and cultivate its end.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to be careful at the outset and steadfast to the end.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「惟德罔小，萬邦惟慶；

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Only virtue, though small—myriad states will have rejoicing;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Even the smallest virtue brings rejoicing to the myriad states;

sentences.zh: 惟不德罔大，墜厥宗。」

translations.literal: only lack of virtue, though great—one will topple one's ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: even the greatest lack of virtue will bring down one's ancestral line."

sentences.zh: 甚可懼也。

translations.literal: This is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly something to dread.

sentences.zh: 夫驕奢起於親貴，綱紀亂於寵幸。

translations.literal: Now arrogance and extravagance arise from those of rank and kin; norms and discipline are disrupted by favored intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Pride and extravagance spring from kin of high station; order collapses when favorites are indulged.

sentences.zh: 禁之於親貴，則天下從；

translations.literal: Prohibiting it among those of rank and kin, then all under heaven will follow;
translations.idiomatic: Restrain it among the royal kin and the realm will follow;

sentences.zh: 制之於寵幸，則天下畏。

translations.literal: controlling it among favored intimates, then all under heaven will fear.
translations.idiomatic: check it among favored intimates and the realm will stand in awe.

sentences.zh: 親貴為而不禁，寵幸撓而不制，故政不常，令不一，則奸詐起而暴亂生焉，雖朝施暮戮，而法不行矣。

translations.literal: When those of rank and kin act yet are not prohibited, when favored intimates obstruct yet are not controlled, therefore government is not constant and orders are not unified—then deceit and fraud arise and violent disorder is born. Even if punishments are meted out morning and evening, the law cannot be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: When kin of rank do as they please unchecked, and favorites interfere without restraint, policy grows inconsistent and commands contradict one another. Fraud flourishes and violence erupts—and even daily executions cannot make the law hold.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲親與愛，莫若安之福之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to show kinship and affection, there is nothing better than securing them in peace and blessing them with fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes truly to love your kin, nothing is better than securing their peace and conferring true blessing.

sentences.zh: 夫寵祿之過，罪之階也，謂安之邪？

translations.literal: Excessive favor and salary—this is the stairway to guilt—is this called securing in peace?
translations.idiomatic: Excessive favor and stipend are the steps to guilt—is that securing peace?

sentences.zh: 驕奢之淫，危之梯也，謂福之邪？

translations.literal: The excess of arrogance and extravagance—this is the ladder to peril—is this called blessing with fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Indulgence in pride and luxury is the ladder to ruin—is that conferring blessing?

sentences.zh: 前事不忘，後之師也。

translations.literal: Not forgetting what went before is the teacher for what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: To remember the past is the teacher of the future.

sentences.zh: 陛下敷求俊哲，使朝夕納誨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should widely seek the wise and talented and have them every morning and evening offer admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should seek out the wise and have them offer counsel morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 其有逆於耳、謬於心者，無速罰，姑求之道；

translations.literal: When there are words that offend the ear or seem wrong in the mind, do not hasten to punish—provisional seek whether they accord with the Way;
translations.idiomatic: When advice is harsh on the ear or unsettling to the mind, do not punish in haste—first ask whether it accords with the Way;

sentences.zh: 順於耳、便於身者，無急賞，姑求之非道。

translations.literal: when words agree with the ear and are convenient to oneself, do not hasten to reward—provisional seek whether they depart from the Way.
translations.idiomatic: and when words are pleasing to hear and easy to follow, do not reward in haste—first ask whether they diverge from the Way.

sentences.zh: 羞淫巧者拒之，則淫巧息；

translations.literal: Reject those skilled in lewd artifice and they will be ashamed to advance—then lewd artifice ceases;
translations.idiomatic: Reject those who trade in lewd trickery and such trickery will die away;

sentences.zh: 進忠讜者賞之，則忠讜進。

translations.literal: reward those who advance loyal and frank counsel, then loyal and frank counsel advances.
translations.idiomatic: reward those who speak loyal and forthright counsel, and such counsel will prevail.

sentences.zh: 臣聞生於富者驕，生於貴者傲。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: those born in wealth are arrogant; those born in nobility are haughty.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those born to wealth grow arrogant and those born to rank grow haughty.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「罔淫於逸，罔遊於樂。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Do not indulge in ease; do not wander in pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Do not wallow in idleness; do not roam in pleasure."

sentences.zh: 今儲宮肇建，王府復啟，願采溫良、博聞、恭儉、忠鯁者為之僚友，仍請東宮置拾遺、補闕，使朝夕講論，出入侍從，授以訓誥，交修不逮。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince's palace has just been established and princely establishments are again opened. I wish that gentle, learned, reverent, frugal, loyal, and upright men be selected as their associates. I further request that the Eastern Palace establish Reminder and Supplementation officers, so that morning and evening they lecture and discuss, going in and out in attendance, imparting instruction and admonition, mutually cultivating what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's establishment has just been formed and princely households reopened. I ask that you select men who are gentle, learned, reverent, frugal, loyal, and outspoken to serve as their companions, and that the Eastern Palace be given Reminder and Supplementation officers to lecture morning and evening, attend them in and out, impart instruction, and help correct their deficiencies.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞「馳騁畋獵，令人發狂」。

translations.literal: Your servant also heard: "Galloping in the hunt drives a man to frenzy."
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that "galloping after the hunt drives a man to madness."

sentences.zh: 今貴戚打球擊鼓，飛鷹奔犬，狎比宵人，盤遊藪澤。

translations.literal: Now noble kin play ball and beat drums, fly hawks and run dogs, draw close to night-roving men, and roam endlessly in marshes and swamps.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial kin play ball and beat drums, fly hawks and run dogs, consort with night-wandering idlers, and roam the marshes without rest.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「內作色荒，外作禽荒。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Within, making lust the waste; without, making birds the waste.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Within, sensual indulgence; without, hunting frenzy."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下誕降謀訓，勸以學業，示之以好惡，陳之以成敗，則長享福祿矣。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty bestow your planning and instruction, encourage them in study, show them likes and dislikes, set forth success and failure for them—then they will long enjoy salary and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to impart counsel and instruction, urge them in their studies, show them what to love and what to hate, and set before them examples of success and failure—then they may long enjoy wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 臣聞「富不與驕期而驕自至，驕不與罪期而罪自至，罪不與死期而死自至」。

translations.literal: Your servant heard: "Wealth does not make an appointment with arrogance, yet arrogance arrives of itself; arrogance does not make an appointment with guilt, yet guilt arrives of itself; guilt does not make an appointment with death, yet death arrives of itself."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard, "Wealth does not plan for pride, yet pride comes of itself; pride does not plan for guilt, yet guilt comes of itself; guilt does not plan for death, yet death comes of itself."

sentences.zh: 頃韋庶人、安樂公主、武延秀等可謂貴且寵矣，權侔人主，威震天下。

translations.literal: Recently the commoner consort Wei, Princess Anle, Wu Yanxiu, and others can be said to have been noble and favored; their power matched the sovereign, their authority shook all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the commoner consort Wei, Princess Anle, Wu Yanxiu, and the like were as honored and favored as anyone could be—their power rivaled the emperor's and their authority shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 然怙侈滅德，神怒人棄，豈不謂愛之太極、富之太多乎？

translations.literal: Yet relying on extravagance they destroyed virtue; gods were angered and men abandoned them—is this not called loving them to the extreme and enriching them too much?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they relied on extravagance and forfeited virtue; the gods were angered and men forsook them. Was that not loving them to excess and enriching them too abundantly?

sentences.zh: 「殷鑒不遠，在夏後之世。」

translations.literal: "The mirror of Yin is not far; it is in the age of the Xia's successor.
translations.idiomatic: "The mirror of the Yin dynasty is not far off—it is in the age that succeeded the Xia."

sentences.zh: 今陛下何勸？

translations.literal: What then should Your Majesty encourage today?
translations.idiomatic: What, then, should Your Majesty take for encouragement?

sentences.zh: 其皇祖謀訓之則乎！

translations.literal: Should it not be the planning and instruction of your imperial grandfather!
translations.idiomatic: The counsels and admonitions of your imperial grandfather!

sentences.zh: 陛下何懲？

translations.literal: What should Your Majesty take as warning?
translations.idiomatic: And what should you take as a warning?

sentences.zh: 其孝和寵任之失乎！

translations.literal: Should it not be the errors of Xiaozong's favor and employment!
translations.idiomatic: The errors of Emperor Xiaozong's indulgence of favorites!

sentences.zh: 故愛而知其惡，憎而知其善。

translations.literal: Therefore in loving, know their evil; in detesting, know their good.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore love them yet know their faults; dislike them yet recognize their virtues.

sentences.zh: 夫寵愛之心未有能免，要去其太甚，閑之以禮，則可矣。

translations.literal: As for the heart's favor and love, none can wholly avoid it; what is needed is to remove its excess and restrain it with ritual—then it will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Affection cannot wholly be suppressed, but its excess can be removed and it can be bounded by ritual—and that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 諸王、公主、駙馬，陛下之所親愛也，矯枉監戒，宜在厥初，使居寵思危，觀過務善。

translations.literal: The various princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law are those Your Majesty loves and cherishes. Correcting deviation and overseeing with warning should be at the beginning, so that dwelling in favor they think of peril, observing faults they strive for good.
translations.idiomatic: The princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law are those Your Majesty holds dear. Correction and vigilant admonition should begin at the outset, so that in enjoying favor they remember danger and, seeing faults, strive for the good.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「三風十愆，卿士有一於身，家必喪，邦君有一於身，國心亡。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "The three vices and ten faults—if a minister or grandee has one of them in his person, his family will surely perish; if the lord of a state has one of them in his person, the state's heart will perish.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Of the three depravities and ten faults—if a minister has even one in his person, his house is doomed; if a ruler has even one in his person, his state is lost."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下黜奢僭驕怠，進樸素行業，以勖其非心。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty dismiss extravagance, usurpation, arrogance, and idleness; advance plainness, simplicity, conduct, and calling—to admonish what is improper in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to reject extravagance, presumption, pride, and sloth; promote plainness and upright conduct—to restrain what is improper in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 臣聞「常厥德，保厥位；

translations.literal: Your servant heard: "Constantly maintaining his virtue, he preserves his position;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: "He who constantly keeps his virtue preserves his position;

sentences.zh: 厥德匪常，九有以亡」。

translations.literal: his virtue not constant—the nine regions thereby perish."
translations.idiomatic: he whose virtue is not constant—the myriad domains are lost."

sentences.zh: 願陛下不作無益，不啟私門，不差刑，不濫賞，則惟德是輔，惟人之懷，天祿永終矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty not to do what is without benefit, not to open private doors, not to misapply punishments, not to lavish rewards in excess—then only virtue will be assisted, only men will be embraced, and Heaven's salary will end forever.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty undertake nothing useless, open no back channels, misapply no punishment, and grant no reward without cause—then virtue alone will be your support, the people alone your concern, and Heaven's blessing will endure without end.

sentences.zh: 睿宗善之，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong approved of it and appointed him Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong was pleased and appointed him Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 開元中，轉殿中侍御史，監嶺南選。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan, Ze was transferred to palace attendant censor and supervised selections in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, Ze was transferred to palace attendant censor and supervised selections in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 時市舶使、右威衛中郎將周慶立造奇器以進，澤上書曰：「『不見可欲，使心不亂』，是知見可欲而心必亂矣。

translations.literal: At the time, Zhou Qingli, maritime trade commissioner and Zhonglangjiang of the Right Awesome Guard, made strange devices and presented them. Ze submitted a memorial saying, “‘Do not show what can be desired, so that the heart will not be disordered’; from this we know that if what can be desired is seen, the heart will certainly be disordered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Zhou Qingli, maritime trade commissioner and Zhonglangjiang of the Right Awesome Guard, made strange devices and presented them. Ze submitted a memorial saying, “‘Do not show what can be desired, so that the heart will not be disordered’; from this we know that if what can be desired is seen, the heart will certainly be disordered.

sentences.zh: 慶立雕制詭物，造作奇器，用浮巧爲珍玩，以譎怪爲異寶，乃治國之巨蠹，明王所宜嚴罰者也。

translations.literal: Qingli carves and fashions bizarre objects and makes strange devices, treating superficial cleverness as precious toys and deceitful oddities as rare treasures. This is a great borer in the governance of the state, one whom an enlightened king should punish severely.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli carves and fashions bizarre objects and makes strange devices, treating superficial cleverness as precious toys and deceitful oddities as rare treasures. This is a great borer in the governance of the state, one whom an enlightened king should punish severely.

sentences.zh: 昔露臺無費，明君不忍；象箸非大，忠臣憤嘆。

translations.literal: Formerly, although the Dew Terrace had not yet incurred expense, an enlightened ruler could not bear to build it; ivory chopsticks were not a great matter, yet loyal ministers sighed in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, although the Dew Terrace had not yet incurred expense, an enlightened ruler could not bear to build it; ivory chopsticks were not a great matter, yet loyal ministers sighed in indignation.

sentences.zh: 慶立求媚聖意，搖蕩上心。

translations.literal: Qingli seeks to flatter the sage will and shake the ruler’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli seeks to flatter the sage will and shake the ruler’s heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下信而使之乎，是宣淫於天下；慶立矯而爲之乎，是禁典之所無赦。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty trusted him and had him do this, then this proclaims excess to the realm; if Qingli falsely acted on his own, then this is something the prohibitory statutes do not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty trusted him and had him do this, then this proclaims excess to the realm; if Qingli falsely acted on his own, then this is something the prohibitory statutes do not pardon.

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，固宜昭宣菲薄，廣示節儉，豈可以怪好示四方哉！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly taken the throne and surely should make plain modesty manifest and broadly display frugality. How can you show strange pleasures to the four quarters?”
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly taken the throne and surely should make plain modesty manifest and broadly display frugality. How can you show strange pleasures to the four quarters?”

sentences.zh: 書奏，玄宗稱善。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Xuanzong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Xuanzong praised it.

sentences.zh: 歷遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Ze was promoted successively to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was promoted successively to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 爲鄭州刺史，未行，卒，贈兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Zhengzhou, but before he set out he died and was posthumously presented as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Zhengzhou, but before he set out he died and was posthumously presented as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 澤從祖範、奭。

translations.literal: Ze's collateral granduncles were Fan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ze's junior granduncles were Liu Fan and Liu Shi.

sentences.zh: 範，貞觀中為侍御史，時吳王恪好田獵，範彈治之。

translations.literal: Fan, during the Zhenguan era, was Attending Censor. At the time Prince Wu of Wu Ke liked field hunting; Fan impeached and prosecuted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan served as Attending Censor under the Zhenguan reign. When Prince Wu of Wu, Li Ke, was devoted to hunting, Fan impeached him.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「權萬紀不能輔道恪，罪當死。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "Quan Wanji could not assist and instruct Ke—his crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "Quan Wanji failed to counsel and guide Li Ke—a capital offense."

sentences.zh: 範進曰：「房玄齡事陛下，猶不能諫止畋獵，豈宜獨罪萬紀？」

translations.literal: Fan advanced and said: "Fang Xuanling served Your Majesty yet could not remonstrate and stop the hunt—how can Wanji alone be punished?
translations.idiomatic: Fan stepped forward: "Fang Xuanling served Your Majesty yet could not dissuade you from hunting. Why should Wanji alone bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，拂衣起。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, brushed his robes and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry, flung aside his robes, and rose to leave.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召謂曰：「何廷折我？」

translations.literal: Before long, [the emperor] summoned [Fan] and said to him, "Why did you rebut me in court?
translations.idiomatic: After a while the emperor summoned Fan and asked, "Why did you contradict me openly in court?"

sentences.zh: 範謝曰：「主聖則臣直，陛下仁明，臣敢不盡愚？」

translations.literal: Fan apologized, saying, "When the ruler is sage, then ministers are upright. Your Majesty is benevolent and enlightened—how dare I not speak my utmost foolishness?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan apologized: "When the sovereign is wise, his ministers speak plainly. Your Majesty is benevolent and clear-sighted; how could I fail to speak my mind?"

sentences.zh: 帝乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon relented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger then subsided.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，歷尚書右丞、揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong, he successively served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he served in succession as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command.

sentences.zh: 奭字子邵。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Zishao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Zishao.

sentences.zh: 以父隋時使高麗卒焉，故往迎喪，號踴盡哀，為夷人所慕。

translations.literal: Because his father had died on a Sui mission to Goguryeo, he went to fetch the coffin home, wailing and stamping in the utmost grief, and was admired by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father had died on a Sui embassy to Goguryeo, so he traveled to bring the coffin home, wailing and beating the ground in deepest mourning—a display the foreigners admired.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he rose through repeated promotions to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 外孫為皇后，遷中書侍郎，進中書令。

translations.literal: When his grandson's wife became empress, he was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat and advanced to Grand Counselor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After his grandson's wife became empress, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and then promoted to Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 皇后挾媚道覺，罷為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The empress was discovered practicing sorcery; he was removed and made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress was caught using witchcraft, he was dismissed from the chancellorship and appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 後廢，貶愛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, when she was deposed, he was demoted to Prefect of Ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress was later deposed, he was demoted to prefect of Ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗等構奭通宮掖，謀行鴆毒，與褚遂良朋黨，罪大逆。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong and others framed Yi for consorting with the inner palace, plotting poison, and forming a faction with Chu Suiliang—the crime of great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong and others fabricated charges that Yi had liaised with the inner palace, plotted poisoning, and banded together with Chu Suiliang, branding him guilty of high treason.

sentences.zh: 遣使殺之，沒其家，期以上親並流嶺表，奭房隸桂州為奴婢。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to kill him; his property was confiscated; relatives within five degrees were all exiled beyond the mountain passes, and Yi's household was enslaved in Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was dispatched to execute him, his estate was confiscated, all relatives within five degrees of kin were exiled south of the Ling, and members of Yi's household were reduced to bondage in Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，乃復官爵，子孫親屬緣坐者悉免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, his offices and titles were restored, and all descendants and kin punished by association were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenlong period his rank and titles were restored, and every descendant and kinsman implicated in the case was released from punishment.

sentences.zh: 開元初，澤兄渙為中書舍人，上言：「臣從伯祖奭，去顯慶三年與褚遂良等五門同被譴戮，雖被原雪，而子孫殆盡，唯曾孫無忝客籍龔州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, Ze's elder brother Huan was Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and submitted a memorial: "Your subject's grand-uncle Yi, in the third year of Xianqing, was condemned and executed together with Chu Suiliang and four other clans. Although he was later cleared, his descendants were nearly wiped out; only his great-grandson Wutian remains registered as a guest resident in Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign, Ze's elder brother Huan, then Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, memorialized: "My grand-uncle Yi, in Xianqing 3 (658), was condemned and executed along with Chu Suiliang and four other families. Though later exonerated, his line was all but extinguished; only his great-grandson Wutian still lives as a registered guest in Gong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陛下先天後詔書，嘗任宰相家並錄其後。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's edicts after the Xiantian and later reigns have sometimes enrolled the descendants of former chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's edicts from the Xiantian period onward have at times restored the descendants of former chief ministers to office.

sentences.zh: 況臣之伯祖無辜被誅，今槁窆未還，後嗣僑處，願許伯祖歸葬，孤孫北遷。」

translations.literal: Moreover, my grand-uncle was executed though innocent; his dried coffin has not yet been returned, and his orphaned descendants live in exile. I beg that my grand-uncle be allowed burial in his homeland and that the lone grandson be permitted to move north.
translations.idiomatic: My grand-uncle was put to death though guiltless; his coffin still lies unburied, and his orphaned descendants remain in exile. I beg leave to bring his remains home for burial and to let the lone grandson return north."

sentences.zh: 於是詔無忝護奭柩歸鄉里，官給喪事。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Wutian to escort Yi's coffin back to his native place, with the state providing funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed Wutian to escort Yi's coffin back to his home district, with official funds for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 無忝後歷潭州都督。

translations.literal: Wutian later served as Area Commander of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wutian later served as military commissioner of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 馮元常

translations.literal: Feng Yuanchang
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuanchang

sentences.zh: 馮元常，相州安陽人，其先蓋長樂信都著姓。

translations.literal: Feng Yuanchang was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture; his forebears were probably a distinguished clan of Xindu in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuanchang, a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture, came from what was likely a prominent clan of Xindu in Changle.

sentences.zh: 曾祖子琮，北齊右僕射。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zicong was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs in Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zicong had been Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 叔祖慈明，有文辭，仕隋為內史舍人。
