translations.literal: His grand-uncle Ciming was skilled in literary composition and served the Sui as Drafting Attendant within the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-uncle Ciming, a man of literary talent, served the Sui as Drafting Attendant within the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奉詔討李密，為密將所縛，身數創，密厚禮之，情謂曰：「東都危蹙，我欲率四方賢豪建功業，幸公同之。」

translations.literal: Ordered to campaign against Li Mi, he was bound by one of Mi's generals and suffered many wounds. Mi treated him generously and said earnestly, "The Eastern Capital is in peril; I wish to lead the worthies of the four quarters to achieve merit—may you join me.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to suppress Li Mi, he was captured by one of Mi's generals after sustaining many wounds. Mi treated him with honor and pleaded, "The Eastern Capital is in dire straits. I mean to rally the worthy men of the realm to build an enterprise—will you stand with me?"

sentences.zh: 慈明曰：「公家事先帝，名在王室，乃挾玄感舉兵，亡命至今，復圖反噬，何耶？」

translations.literal: Ciming said, "Your clan served the late emperor and your name stands in the royal house. Yet you followed Yang Xuangan in raising troops, fled as an outlaw until now, and again plot rebellion—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Ciming replied, "Your house served the late emperor; your name belongs to the imperial clan. Yet you followed Yang Xuangan in rebellion, have lived as a fugitive until now, and again seek to turn on your sovereign—how can that be?"

sentences.zh: 密囚之。

translations.literal: Mi imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 俄為翟護所殺。

translations.literal: Before long he was killed by Zhai Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was killed by Zhai Hu.

sentences.zh: 武德初，贈吏部尚書，謚壯武。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era, [Ciming] was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wude reign he was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 元常舉明經及第，調浚儀尉。

translations.literal: Yuanchang passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Commandant of Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed commandant of Junyi.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，擢累監察御史、劍南道巡察使，興利除害，蜀人順賴。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong he was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor and Touring Commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit, removing harm and advancing benefit so that the people of Shu relied on him in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he rose through repeated promotions to Investigating Censor and Touring Commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit, where he removed abuses and promoted what was beneficial until the people of Shu came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗密諫帝中宮權重，宜少抑，帝雖置其計，而內然之，由是為武后所惡。

translations.literal: He once secretly remonstrated that the power of the empress in the inner palace was too great and ought to be somewhat restrained. Although the emperor set aside his plan, inwardly he approved it, and for this Empress Wu came to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: He once privately urged the emperor that the empress's power in the inner palace was excessive and should be curbed. The emperor did not adopt the proposal, yet inwardly he agreed—and from this Empress Wu came to detest him.

sentences.zh: 元常在職脩舉，識鑒澄遠，帝委遇特厚。

translations.literal: Yuanchang in office cultivated what should be cultivated; his discernment was clear and far-reaching, and the emperor entrusted and favored him in special measure.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yuanchang upheld proper conduct and his judgment was lucid and far-sighted; the emperor relied on him with exceptional trust.

sentences.zh: 及不豫，詔平章百司奏事。

translations.literal: When [the emperor] fell ill, an edict made him equal participant in deciding memorials from the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew ill, an edict named him to join in deciding memorials from every department.

sentences.zh: 武后擅朝，嵩陽令樊文進瑞石，後暴石朝堂示百官。

translations.literal: Empress Wu monopolized the court; Songyang Magistrate Fan Wenjin presented an auspicious stone, and the empress displayed the stone in the court hall before the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: With Empress Wu dominating the court, Songyang Magistrate Fan Wenjin presented a "propitious" stone, which the empress had displayed in the hall before the assembled officials.

sentences.zh: 元常奏石妄偽，不可以示群臣。

translations.literal: Yuanchang memorialized that the stone was falsely fabricated and must not be shown to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang submitted that the stone was a forgery and should not be displayed to the ministers.

sentences.zh: 後怒，出為隴州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress was angered and sent him out as Prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, enraged, had him transferred out to serve as prefect of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會天下嶽牧集乾陵，後不欲元常得會，故道徙眉州刺史。

translations.literal: When all the circuit governors gathered at Qianling, the empress did not want Yuanchang to attend the meeting and therefore rerouted him, transferring him to Prefect of Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When governors from across the empire assembled at Qianling, the empress did not want Yuanchang present and had his route diverted, transferring him instead to prefect of Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劍南有光火盜，夜掠人，晝伏山谷。

translations.literal: In Jiannan there were torch-bandits who plundered people by night and hid by day in the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiannan there were "torch-and-fire" bandits who raided by night and lay hidden in the valleys by day.

sentences.zh: 元常喻以恩信，約悔過自新，賊相率脫甲面縛。

translations.literal: Yuanchang instructed them with kindness and trust, promising that if they repented and reformed themselves the bandits would one after another cast off armor and come bound with faces exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang appealed to them with kindness and good faith, offering amnesty if they repented; the bandits then came forward in succession, stripping off armor and surrendering with hands bound.

sentences.zh: 賊平，轉廣州都督，詔便驛走官。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was transferred to Area Commander of Guang Prefecture, with an edict ordering him to take office at once by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits were pacified he was transferred to military commissioner of Guang Prefecture, with orders to travel by post relay and take up the post immediately.

sentences.zh: 安南酋領李嗣仙殺都護劉延祐，劫州縣，詔元常討之。

translations.literal: The Annan chieftain Li Sixian killed Protector-General Liu Yanyou and raided prefectures and counties; an edict ordered Yuanchang to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The Annam chieftain Li Sixian killed Protector-General Liu Yanyou and plundered prefectures and counties; Yuanchang was ordered to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 率士卒航海，馳檄先示禍福，賊黨多降，元常縱兵斬首惡而還。

translations.literal: Leading troops by sea, he first dispatched proclamations showing fortune and disaster; many of the rebels surrendered, and Yuanchang unleashed his soldiers to behead the ringleaders and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops by sea and first sent out proclamations setting out reward and punishment; many rebels submitted, and Yuanchang then sent his troops to execute the chief culprits before returning.

sentences.zh: 雖有功，猶以拂旨見怨，不錄功。

translations.literal: Although he had merit, because he had offended the empress's wishes he was resented and his achievement was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his success, he had crossed the empress's will and earned her resentment, so his merit went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 凡三徙，終不得至京師，卒為酷吏周興所陷，追赴都，下獄死。

translations.literal: In all he was transferred three times and never reached the capital; in the end he was framed by the cruel official Zhou Xing, summoned to the capital, thrown into prison, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred three times in all, he never reached the capital again. At last the cruel official Zhou Xing framed him; he was summoned to court, thrown into prison, and died there.

sentences.zh: 元常閨門雍睦，有禮法，雖小功喪不禦私室。

translations.literal: Yuanchang's inner household was harmonious and observed ritual propriety; even during mourning for a distant relative he would not enter a private chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household Yuanchang maintained harmony and strict ritual propriety; even during mourning for a distant kinsman he would not enter a private room.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，旌其家，大署曰「忠臣之門」。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era his family was honored, and a large inscription reading "Gate of Loyal Ministers" was posted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong period his family was officially honored with a large plaque reading "Gate of Loyal Ministers."

sentences.zh: 天下高其節，凡名族皆願通婚。

translations.literal: The empire admired his integrity; every eminent clan wished to marry with his house.
translations.idiomatic: The realm held his integrity in high esteem, and distinguished families everywhere sought marriage ties with his house.

sentences.zh: 從弟元淑，及後時，歷清漳、浚儀、始平三縣令，右善去惡，人稱為神明。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Yuanshu, in Empress Wu's time, successively served as magistrate of Qingzhang, Junyi, and Shiping—promoting the good and removing the evil, and was called divine by the people.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Yuanshu, under Empress Wu, served in succession as magistrate of Qingzhang, Junyi, and Shiping, where he promoted the good and punished the wicked until the people hailed him as a spirit of justice.

sentences.zh: 與奴仆日一食，馬日一秣，所至不挈妻子，斥奉余以給貧窮。

translations.literal: He and his servants ate one meal a day; his horses were fed one ration a day; wherever he went he did not bring his wife and children, and he spent his surplus salary to aid the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He took one meal a day with his servants and fed each horse a single ration; he never brought wife or children on his postings, and gave away his surplus salary to the needy.

sentences.zh: 或譏其近名，元淑曰：「吾性也，不為苦。」

translations.literal: Some mocked him for courting reputation; Yuanshu said, "That is my nature—I do not find it bitter.
translations.idiomatic: When some ridiculed him for seeking a name for virtue, Yuanshu said, "That is simply my nature; I do not consider it hardship."

sentences.zh: 中宗降璽書勞勉，付狀史官。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong sent an imperial letter of commendation and had the account delivered to the historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong issued an imperial letter of praise and had the record forwarded to the historiographer.

sentences.zh: 元淑約潔過於元常，然剛直不及也。

translations.literal: Yuanshu in frugality and purity exceeded Yuanchang, yet in blunt uprightness he did not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshu was even more austere and abstemious than Yuanchang, but he fell short of him in forthright integrity.

sentences.zh: 終祠部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 蔣欽緒

translations.literal: Jiang Qinxu
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qinxu

sentences.zh: 蔣欽緒，萊州膠水人。

translations.literal: Jiang Qinxu was a native of Jiaoshui in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qinxu was a native of Jiaoshui in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 頗工文辭，擢進士第，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled in literary composition, passed the jinshi examination, and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in literary composition, he passed the jinshi examination and rose through repeated promotions to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 中宗始親郊，國子祭酒祝欽明建言，皇后應亞獻，欲以媚韋氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong first personally performed the suburban sacrifice, the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Zhu Qinming proposed that the empress should serve as secondary offerer, intending thereby to flatter the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong first performed the suburban sacrifice in person, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Zhu Qinming proposed that the empress serve as secondary offerer—a move meant to curry favor with the Wei clan.

sentences.zh: 天子疑之，詔禮官議。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was doubtful and ordered the ritual officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was uncertain and ordered the ritual specialists to debate the question.

sentences.zh: 眾曲意阿徇，欽緒獨抗言不可，諸儒壯其節。

translations.literal: The multitude bent their words to fawn and comply; Qinxu alone spoke out that it could not be done, and the Confucian scholars admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials twisted their views to flatter and agree, but Qinxu alone protested that it was impermissible, and the ritual scholars admired his fortitude.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 始，韓琬為高郵主簿，使京師，自負其才，有不遇之言題客舍。

translations.literal: At first, when Han Wan was chief clerk of Gaoyou and sent to the capital, confident in his talent he wrote words of unappreciated worth on the wall of a traveler's lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Wan was chief clerk of Gaoyou and traveled to the capital, he was so confident in his talent that he inscribed a complaint about going unrecognized on the wall of a roadside inn.

sentences.zh: 它日，欽緒見之，笑曰：「是子嘆後時耶？」

translations.literal: Another day Qinxu saw it and laughed, saying, "Does this fellow lament that his time has not come?
translations.idiomatic: One day Qinxu saw the inscription and laughed: "Is this man complaining that his hour has not yet arrived?"

sentences.zh: 久之，琬舉賢良方正，欽緒擢其文異等，因謂曰：「朋友之過免未？」

translations.literal: After a long time Wan was recommended as Worthy and Upright, and Qinxu ranked his essay in the highest class; he then said to him, "Is a friend's fault forgiven yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Years later, when Wan was nominated as Worthy and Upright, Qinxu graded his essay in the highest class and then asked him, "Is a friend's fault forgiven now?"

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「今日乃見君子之心。」

translations.literal: Wan said, "Today I have seen the heart of a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Wan replied, "Today I have seen what a true gentleman's heart is like."

sentences.zh: 其務薦引士類此。

translations.literal: His zeal in recommending and advancing scholars was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his zeal in recommending and advancing men of talent.

sentences.zh: 欽緒精治道，馭吏整嚴，雖銖秒罪不貸。

translations.literal: Qinxu was thoroughly versed in the art of governance; in controlling officials he was strict and orderly, and even the smallest offense he would not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Qinxu had mastered the principles of governance; he managed officials with strict discipline and would not overlook even the slightest infraction.

sentences.zh: 出為華州長史。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Administrator of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as chief administrator of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠自晉州被召，過欽緒，欽緒本姻家，因戒曰：「以君才不患不見用，患非分而求耳。」

translations.literal: When Xiao Zhizhong was summoned from Jin Prefecture and passed Qinxu's place, Qinxu, who was related to him by marriage, therefore admonished him, saying, "With your talent you need not fear going unused—what you should fear is seeking what is not your due.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zhizhong was recalled from Jin Prefecture and stopped to see Qinxu—a kinsman by marriage—Qinxu warned him: "With your ability you need not worry about going unrecognized; what you should fear is reaching for what is not rightfully yours."

sentences.zh: 至忠竟及禍。

translations.literal: Zhizhong in the end met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong ultimately came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，以御史中丞錄河南囚，宣尉百姓，振窮乏。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan he, as Assistant Censor-in-Chief, reviewed prisoners in Henan, announced comfort to the people, and relieved the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 (725) he served as Assistant Censor-in-Chief reviewing prisoners in Henan, proclaiming reassurance to the people and relieving the poor.

sentences.zh: 徙吏部侍郎，歷汴、魏二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and successively served as Prefect of Bian and Wei; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then served in succession as prefect of Bian and Wei before his death.

sentences.zh: 性孤潔自守，唯與賈曾、郭利貞相友雲。

translations.literal: By nature solitary, pure, and self-restrained, he maintained friendship only with Jia Zeng and Guo Lizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Solitary, upright, and self-contained by nature, he kept close company with only Jia Zeng and Guo Lizhen.

sentences.zh: 子沇，亦專潔博學，少有名。

translations.literal: His son Mian was likewise pure and broadly learned and was famous while still young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mian was equally upright and widely learned and won renown while still young.

sentences.zh: 以孝廉授洛陽尉，遷監察御史，與兄演、溶、弟清俱為才吏，有名天寶間。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he was appointed Luoyang Assistant Magistrate, then Investigating Censor; together with his elder brothers Yan and Rong and his younger brother Qing he was an able official, all famous in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, he was appointed assistant magistrate of Luoyang and then Investigating Censor; he and his elder brothers Yan and Rong and his younger brother Qing were all capable officials renowned during the Tianbao period.

sentences.zh: 始，河南尹韓朝宗、裴迥嘗委訊覆檢句，而處事平，剖斷精允，群寮莫能望也。

translations.literal: At first, when Henan Intendant Han Chaozong and Pei Jiong entrusted him with reviewing and checking cases, his handling was even-handed and his judgments precise and fair, and none of the staff could match him.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan Intendant Han Chaozong and Pei Jiong first put him in charge of reviewing cases, his decisions were even-handed and his rulings exact, and none of his colleagues could equal him.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，歷陸渾、盩厔、咸陽、高陵四縣令，美政流行，長老紀焉。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era he successively served as magistrate of Luhun, Zhouzhi, Xianyang, and Gaoling; good governance spread abroad and the elders recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan reign he served in succession as magistrate of Luhun, Zhouzhi, Xianyang, and Gaoling, where his excellent administration was widely praised and remembered by the elders.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀軍出其縣，敕麾下曰：「蔣沇，賢令，供億當有素，士得蔬飯足矣，毋撓其清也！」

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi's army passed through his county, he ordered his subordinates, saying, "Jiang Mian is a worthy magistrate; supplies for the army should already be in order—let the men have plain vegetables and rice, that is enough; do not disturb his integrity!
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi's army marched through his county, he instructed his commanders: "Magistrate Jiang Mian is a man of worth; his provisions should already be in good order. Plain vegetables and rice are enough for the troops—do not disturb his integrity!"

sentences.zh: 遷長安令，以刑部郎中兼侍御史，領渭橋運出納使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Chang'an and, as Director in the Ministry of Justice concurrently Serving Censor, headed the Weiqiao transport disbursement office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Chang'an and, as Director in the Ministry of Justice with concurrent duty as Attending Censor, oversaw disbursements at the Weiqiao transport depot.

sentences.zh: 元載持政，守道士類不遷，沇以故滯郎位，不得調。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai held power, upright officials were generally not promoted; for this reason Mian remained stuck in a director's post and could not be reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan Zai's dominance, upright officials were seldom promoted, and Mian for that reason languished in a director's post without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 常袞代相，聞士議恨沇屈，故擢御史中丞、東都副留守。

translations.literal: When Chang Gun replaced [Yuan Zai] as chancellor, hearing that scholars resented Mian's being wronged, he therefore promoted him to Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Eastern Capital Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Gun replaced Yuan Zai as chancellor, hearing scholars complain that Mian had been treated unjustly, he promoted him to Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Eastern Capital Intendant.

sentences.zh: 再遷大理卿，持法明審，號稱職。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, holding the law with clarity and exactness, and was said to fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, where he applied the law with clarity and precision and was regarded as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，沇奔行在，為賊所拘，欲誘署偽職，沇絕食不應命，竄伏里中，不復見。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Mian rushed to the traveling court; he was seized by the rebels, who wished to entice him into accepting a false appointment. Mian refused food and would not obey; he hid in the lanes and was seen no more.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong withdrew to Fengtian, Mian hurried to the mobile court but was captured by rebels who tried to lure him into a puppet appointment. He refused food and would not submit, then went into hiding in the alleys and was seen no more.

sentences.zh: 京師平，乃出，擢右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified he came forth and was promoted to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered he emerged and was promoted to Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 清，舉明經中第，調鞏丞。

translations.literal: Qing passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Qing passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Gong.

sentences.zh: 東京留守李靰賢之，表為判官。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital Intendant Li Cheng admired him and recommended him as judge.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital Intendant Li Cheng admired him and recommended him as judge on his staff.

sentences.zh: 與憕同死安祿山亂，贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died together with Li Cheng in the An Lushan rebellion and was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died alongside Li Cheng during the An Lushan rebellion and was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敬宗時，錄其孫鄅為伊闕令。

translations.literal: During Emperor Jingzong's reign his grandson Yu was enrolled as Magistrate of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Jingzong's reign his grandson Yu was appointed magistrate of Yique.

sentences.zh: 初，清蒙難，以秩卑不及謚。

translations.literal: At first, because Qing suffered calamity while his rank was low, he did not receive a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Qing met his death while still in a low post, no posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 太和初，其出吏部郎中王高言之朝，追謚曰忠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era his descendant Wang Gao, a Deputy Director in the Ministry of Personnel, spoke of the matter at court, and a posthumous title of Zhong was granted in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe reign his descendant Wang Gao, Deputy Director in the Ministry of Personnel, raised the matter at court, and Qing was posthumously given the title Zhong ("Loyal").
